summary: Khayutin proves the mixing conjecture of Michel and Venkatesh — that the joint packets {(z, σ.z) : z ∈ P} of CM points equidistribute in the product of two modular curves when the minimal norm 𝔑 of an integral ideal in the class of the twist tends to infinity — under two hypotheses: that two fixed primes p_1, p_2 split in every CM field, and that no Dedekind zeta function in the sequence has an exceptional Landau–Siegel zero. He works adelically, with a form G of PGL_2 over Q and self-joinings of periodic toral measures on [(G × G)(A)], and proves that every weak-* limit is (G × G)(A)^+-invariant, a conclusion that cannot be improved because the joint packets may miss connected components; a companion proposition computes exactly which combinations of Haar measures occur. The previous result, of Ellenberg, Michel and Venkatesh, required 𝔑 ≪ |D|^{1/2−η}, which fails for most twists; the new proof removes that restriction by replacing the search for a small Hecke correspondence containing the packet with a direct estimate. The argument has two halves. Measure rigidity, through the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss classification of joinings of higher-rank torus actions, shows that every limit is a convex combination of algebraic measures each of which is either Haar or supported on a homogeneous Hecke set [G^Δ(A)^+ξ]. The second half eliminates the Hecke possibility by bounding the pair cross-correlation of the packet with any Hecke correspondence: unfolding the automorphic kernel gives a geometric expansion into relative orbital integrals indexed by the rational points of the GIT double quotient G^Δ\(G × G)/T^Δ; explicit coordinates for the quaternion algebra split by the CM field turn each orbit into a pair of integral ideals of the quadratic order, with multiplicity bounded by the 2-torsion of the Picard group; and the resulting shifted convolution of ideal-counting functions is a sum along the values of the reduced norm form of the twisting ideal over the lattice points of an ellipse whose eccentricity is controlled by 𝔑. A general two-dimensional sieve, developed from scratch in Section 8, bounds that sum by the expected order with a saving p_1^{-2n} over Bowen balls of the diagonal flow, and the absence of a Siegel zero is used once, to pass from a sum of the ideal-counting function to the class number through L(1, χ_E). The n-fold version and the consequence for Galois orbits of special points on products of quaternionic Shimura varieties follow. In the atlas, GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans lattice-point estimates and the ergodic machinery 'needed for Oppenheim/Duke-type arithmetic applications', AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.1–AA.4 the adelic quotients, reduction theory and strong approximation, HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.0 quadratic orders with their Picard groups and ring class fields, SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.0–SV.2 sieve data and the large sieve, AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1 and AN.5 Dirichlet L-functions and multiplicative functions, ShimuraVarieties V4 the reciprocity formula at special points, and the Tau Ceti roadmaps on global number fields and on quadratic form invariants orders, Picard groups and quaternion algebras. Nothing plans joinings, measure rigidity, toral packets, homogeneous Hecke sets, relative orbital integrals for (G^Δ, T^Δ), or the mixing conjecture. After the review, of the 124 items 2 are planned and 122 are routed: 82 to a Part II of GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic, 17 as a source of the sieve roadmap, 18 as a source of HE.0, 3 as a source of AA.4 and 2 as a source of GN.2/GN.4.

items.name: The mixing conjecture of Michel and Venkatesh
items.statement: Let Y be a complex modular curve and let P_i ⊂ Y be a sequence of packets of CM points, each a principal homogeneous space of Pic(Λ_i) for the CM order Λ_i of discriminant D_i < 0. For each i fix σ_i ∈ Pic(Λ_i) and set P_i^joint = {(z, σ_i.z) : z ∈ P_i} ⊂ Y × Y, with μ_i^joint the normalised counting measure on it. Set 𝔑_i = min{Nr(𝔞) : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ_i invertible, 𝔞 ∈ σ_i}. If 𝔑_i → ∞ then μ_i^joint converges weak-* to m_Y × m_Y.
items.locator: §1.1, Conjecture 1.1 (Mixing Conjecture), p. 146 (arXiv v3: Conjecture 1)
items.note: The conjecture the paper proves under additional hypotheses. Duke's theorem, that the counting measure on a single packet equidistributes when |D_i| → ∞, is the one-fold statement it refines; GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans equidistribution and the ergodic machinery 'needed for Oppenheim/Duke-type arithmetic applications' but names no joint statement.

items.name: Equidistribution of Galois orbits of special points
items.statement: Let X be a finite product of complex modular curves and {x_i} a sequence of special points, i.e. each coordinate is a CM point, with μ_i the normalised counting measure on the finite Galois orbit of x_i. If {x_i} has finite intersection with every proper special subvariety of X, then μ_i converges weak-* to the uniform probability measure on X. This conjecture implies the André–Oort conjecture for products of modular curves, and the mixing conjecture implies a special case of it through the reciprocity map of class field theory.
items.locator: §1.1, Conjecture 1.2 with footnote 2 and the following paragraph on André–Oort, pp. 146–147 (arXiv v3: Conjecture 2)
items.note: The geometric conjecture the mixing conjecture feeds. LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6 plans o-minimality and unlikely intersections, hence the Pila–Zannier route to André–Oort, but the equidistribution statement is of a different nature and, as the paper notes, the Pila–Zannier strategy sheds no light on it.

items.name: Main theorem for toral packets
items.statement: Let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q, K_f < G(A_f) compact open, K_∞ < G(R) a compact real torus, and Y = G(Q)\G(A)/(K_∞ × K_f). Let P_i ⊂ Ỹ be a sequence of K_∞-invariant toral packets with fundamental discriminant D_i < 0, each a principal homogeneous space for an abelian group C_i with a homomorphism C_i → Pic(Λ_i) to the Picard group of the attached order Λ_i in an imaginary quadratic field E_i. Choose σ_i ∈ C_i and let μ_i^joint be the counting measure on {(z, σ_i.z) : z ∈ P_i} ⊂ Y × Y. Fix primes p_1, p_2 and assume for all i that (1) p_1 and p_2 split in E_i, and (2) the Dedekind zeta function of E_i has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero. If 𝔑_i = min{Nr 𝔞 : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ_i invertible, [𝔞] = [σ_i]} → ∞, then every weak-* limit point of {μ_i^joint} is a convex combination of the uniform probability measures on the connected components of Y × Y.
items.locator: §1.2.1, Theorem 1.3, p. 148 (setting of Ỹ and packets on pp. 147–148) (arXiv v3: Theorem 3 of the introduction, a special case of Theorem 14)
items.note: The paper's headline theorem: the mixing conjecture under two splitting hypotheses and the absence of a Siegel zero, and with no upper bound on 𝔑_i. The conclusion cannot be improved to equidistribution on all of Y × Y, since the joint packets may miss connected components; Proposition 18 computes exactly which limits occur.

items.name: Main theorem for Galois orbits of special points
items.statement: Let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q split over R and let X be a finite product of indefinite Shimura curves relative to G. Let {x_i} be a sequence of special points all of whose coordinates have CM by the same maximal order, with μ_i the counting measure on the Galois orbit of x_i and E_i the CM field. Fix primes p_1, p_2 and assume for all i that p_1, p_2 split in E_i and that the Dedekind zeta function of E_i has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero. If {x_i} has finite intersection with every proper special subvariety then every weak-* limit point of {μ_i} is a convex combination of the uniform probability measures on the connected components of X.
items.locator: §1.2.2, Theorem 1.4, p. 149 (arXiv v3: Theorem 4 of the introduction, restated as Theorem 22)
items.note: The geometric consequence, obtained from the n-fold toral theorem through the reciprocity map of class field theory. ShimuraVarieties V4 plans canonical models and the reciprocity formula at special points and HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.1 the quaternionic curves; the equidistribution statement is not planned.

items.name: Adelic quotients, anisotropy and the simply connected cover
items.statement: For a linear algebraic group M over Q write [M(A)] = M(Q)\M(A). If M is anisotropic over Q, i.e. has no Q-characters to G_m, then [M(A)] carries a unique M(A)-invariant probability measure. For reductive M, M^sc denotes the simply connected cover, an isogeny M^sc → M is fixed, and M(R)^+ is the image of M^sc(R) for a ring R. For a closed subgroup L < M, L^Δ < M × M is the diagonal, and ctr : M × M → M is (g_1, g_2) ↦ g_1^{-1}g_2.
items.locator: §2.1, Notation and conventions, items (2), (3), (5), (6), (7), pp. 158–159 (arXiv v3: Section 2.1)
items.note: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.1 constructs adelic points and their functoriality and AA.3 proves that G(F)\G(A)^1 has finite volume together with the compactness criterion for anisotropic groups; the simply connected cover and the subgroup of images of its rational points are part of the reductive-group package AA.4 uses for strong approximation.

items.name: Forms of PGL_2 and their adelic locally homogeneous spaces
items.statement: Let B be a quaternion algebra over Q, Z the centre of B^×, and G = Z\B^×, a form of PGL_2 over Q; every Q-form of PGL_2 arises this way. Then [G(A)] ≅ Z(A)B^×(Q)\B^×(A). For a compact-open K_f < G(A_f), Ỹ = G(Q)\G(A)/K_f is a finite disjoint union of locally homogeneous spaces Γ_δ\G(R) over δ ∈ G(Q)\G(A_f)/K_f, with Γ_δ = G(Q) ∩ δK_fδ^{-1} a congruence lattice.
items.locator: §2.2, display (5), p. 159; decomposition of Ỹ in §1.2.1, p. 147 (arXiv v3: Section 2.2)
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap on quadratic form invariants constructs quaternion algebras with their reduced norm and the split-or-division dichotomy; AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3 supplies the finiteness of G(F)\G(A_f)/K modulo the archimedean connected component that gives the decomposition into locally homogeneous spaces.

items.name: Maximal orders in B and the compact subgroups K_v
items.statement: Fix a maximal Z-order O ⊂ B(Q). For finite v its v-adic closure O_v is a maximal Z_v-order of B(Q_v), and K_v < G(Q_v) is the image of O_v^×; G(A) and B^×(A) are restricted products with respect to the K_v and O_v. If B splits at a finite v, the maximal orders of B(Q_v) ≅ End_{Q_v}(Q_v^2) are the End_{Z_v}(L) for full-rank Z_v-lattices L, in bijection with the vertices of the Bruhat–Tits tree; O_v^× is a vertex stabiliser and K_v is a special maximal compact-open subgroup. If B ramifies at a finite v, O_v is the unique maximal order (the integral closure of Z_v), O_v^× is normal in B^×(Q_v), and K_v is normal of index 2 in the compact group G(Q_v). At ∞ fix a maximal compact torus K_∞ < G(R). If B(R) is split, fix an algebra isomorphism B(R) ≅ M_2(R) carrying K_∞ to PSO_2(R) (unique up to Ad PGO_2(R)) and let ‖·‖_∞ be the operator norm of the Euclidean norm on R^2, which does not depend on that choice; if B(R) is the Hamilton quaternions, ‖·‖_∞ = √Nrd. Then ‖g^{-1}‖_∞ = ‖g‖_∞/|Nrd g| for g ∈ B^×(R). Set O_∞ = {g ∈ B^×(R) : ‖g‖_∞ ≤ 1}, O_∞^× = {g ∈ B^×(R) : ‖g‖_∞ = 1, Nrd g = 1} (in the split case the orientation-preserving isotropy group of |·|_∞, ≅ SO_2(R)), and Ω̃_∞ = {g ∈ B^×(R) : ‖g^{±1}‖_∞ ≤ 2, Nrd g > 0}, a connected, symmetric, compact identity neighbourhood with O_∞^×Ω̃_∞ = Ω̃_∞O_∞^× = Ω̃_∞ on which 1/4 ≤ Nrd g ≤ 4.
items.locator: §2.2.1 'Maximal order in B(Q)', including (6) and (7), pp. 160–162 (arXiv v3: Section 2.2)
items.note: The archimedean 'maximal order' is the paper's own device: the closed unit ball of the operator norm is only a multiplicative monoid, not a ring, and it is what makes the archimedean orbital integral of Section 5 finite. The non-archimedean half is standard quaternion arithmetic that no layer of the atlas states in this form. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Inherits a mistake of the paper (new issue below): the printed set O_∞^× = {g ∈ B^×(R) : ‖g‖_∞ = 1, Nrd g > 0} is not SO_2(R) and not the isotropy group of |·|_∞ (it contains diag(1, 1/2)); the intended set has Nrd g = 1. The item also omits that ‖·‖_∞ is computed through a fixed isomorphism (B(R), K_∞) ≅ (M_2(R), PSO_2(R)) and that O_∞^×Ω̃_∞ = Ω̃_∞O_∞^× = Ω̃_∞. Same in arXiv v3 and print. Review note on status: Partly planned: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 builds the GL_n building from homothety classes of lattices and names the SL_2 tree as a validation example, which covers 'maximal orders of M_2(Q_v) = End(L) ↔ vertices'. The quaternionic maximal orders and the archimedean monoid O_∞ are not planned; missing is right for the item as a whole.

items.name: The reduced norm and the components of the adelic quotient
items.statement: The reduced norm induces a monomorphism of compact abelian groups Nrd : G(A)/G(A)^+ → A^×/(A^×)², and a monomorphism of double coset spaces G(Q)\G(A)/G(A)^+ → Q^×\A^×/(A^×)². By the Hasse–Schilling–Maass theorem every element of Q^× is a reduced norm when B is split at ∞, and only the positive ones otherwise; so the second map is onto in the split case and has index-2 image otherwise.
items.locator: §2.3 'Simply connected cover', p. 162 (arXiv v3: Section 2.3)
items.note: AA.4 plans strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple groups with the required noncompact local factor, which is what identifies G(A)^+ and its class set; the Hasse–Schilling–Maass norm theorem is quaternion arithmetic in the Tau Ceti quadratic-form roadmap's direction. Review note on status: The 'planned' status is generous. AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4 plans strong approximation but not the reduced-norm description of G(A)/G(A)^+. The Hasse–Schilling–Maass norm theorem is not named in QuadraticFormInvariants layer 2; for B over Q it would follow from the local–global representation theorem for the quaternary norm form (GlobalQuadraticForms layers 5–6). Review: status changed from planned to missing; AA.4 plans strong approximation, not the reduced-norm description of G(A)/G(A)^+ (Hasse–Schilling–Maass), and Tau Ceti QuadraticFormInvariants layer 2 plans the reduced norm but not this description. Routed with items 17 and 21 as a source of AA.4.

items.name: Homogeneous toral sets and toral packets
items.statement: For a maximal torus T < G defined and anisotropic over Q and g ∈ G(A), the set [T(A)g] ⊂ [G(A)] is a homogeneous toral set. It is a right translate of [T(A)] ≅ T(Q)\T(A) and carries a unique probability measure invariant under the right action of H_A := g^{-1}T(A)g, the periodic toral measure. A toral packet P is a finite collection of orbits in Ỹ of a real torus H < G(R) that is the projection of a single adelic torus orbit. The set of H-orbits in P is a principal homogeneous space for a finite abelian group C, a quotient of the idele class group of the attached quadratic field E/Q, and there is a canonical surjection C → Pic(Λ), which is an isomorphism when K_f is maximal.
items.locator: §2.4.1 'Homogeneous sets and periodic measures', p. 163; packets and the group C in §1.2.1, p. 148 and §2.4.2, pp. 163–164 (arXiv v3: Section 2.4)
items.note: The central object, in the sense of Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh. Nothing in the atlas plans toral packets; HE.1 plans CM points on a modular curve as a source of Heegner points, which is the classical special case. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. The periodic toral measure is invariant under the right action of H_A = g^{-1}T(A)g, not 'T(A)-invariant'. [T(A)g] is a right translate, and T(A) does not act on the quotient.

items.name: Local orders attached to a homogeneous toral set
items.statement: With T̃ = E^× for a maximal commutative subalgebra E < B, set Λ_v = E(Q_v) ∩ g_v O_v g_v^{-1} for each place v. For non-archimedean v this is an order in the étale algebra E(Q_v) ≅ E_v; at the archimedean place it is defined by the analogous intersection with O_∞.
items.locator: §2.4.4, Definition 2.1, p. 165 (arXiv v3: Definition 5)
items.note: The local invariants of a homogeneous toral set. The Tau Ceti roadmap on global number fields, layer 11, constructs orders in a number field with their conductors and Picard groups, and HE.0 the quadratic orders O_c = Z + cO_K with their ideals; the orders here are cut out by a quaternionic maximal order and an adelic point, which is not that construction.

items.name: The local orders are almost everywhere maximal
items.statement: For almost all non-archimedean v one has Λ_v = O_{E_v}.
items.locator: §2.4.4, Proposition 2.2, pp. 165–166 (arXiv v3: Proposition 6)
items.note: Finiteness of the conductor, which makes the global order of the next item well defined.

items.name: Local structure and Galois stability of the orders
items.statement: For every non-archimedean v there is 𝔣_v ∈ Z_v with Λ_v = Z_v + 𝔣_vO_{E_v}; the conductor of Λ_v is 𝔣_vO_{E_v} and Λ_v is stable under the Galois action of Gal(E_v/Q_v).
items.locator: §2.4.4, Lemma 2.3, p. 166 (arXiv v3: Lemma 7)
items.note: The local form Z_v + 𝔣_vO_{E_v} is the local analogue of the orders O_c = Z + cO_K that HE.0 plans globally; the Galois stability is what makes the coboundary calculus of Section 4 work. Review note on status: Stays missing. HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.0 and GlobalNumberFields layer 11 plan the global orders Z + cO_K and their conductors, not the local statement.

items.name: Local and global discriminants of a homogeneous toral set
items.statement: (1) For finite v, D_v is the discriminant of the order Λ_v ⊂ E_v; in particular D_v = 1 at every v where E is unramified and Λ_v is maximal. (2) For v = ∞, identify E(R) with R × R or C by the natural topological ring isomorphism (unique up to automorphism), pull back the Lebesgue volume form of the Euclidean norm, let Λ_∞ ⊂ E(R) be the intersection of E(R) with the closed unit ball of ‖·‖_∞ (conjugated by g_∞ as in Definition 2.1: Λ_∞ = E(R) ∩ g_∞O_∞g_∞^{-1}), and set D_∞ = vol(Λ_∞)^2. (3) The discriminant of [T(A)g] is D = ∏_v D_v. The discriminant of the global order Λ is ∏_{v≠∞} D_v. Under (♠), D_∞, D_{p_1} and D_{p_2} are the same for all homogeneous toral sets (Remark 2.5). The paper then asserts D_∞ = 1, although Λ_∞ is a unit disc and the definition as printed gives π^2, so an implicit normalising constant is needed.
items.locator: §2.4.4, Definition 2.4 (with Remark 2.5), p. 166 (arXiv v3: Definition 8)
items.note: The complexity parameter in every statement of the paper. It is the invariant of Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh; the atlas plans discriminants of quadratic orders at HE.0 and in the Tau Ceti orders layer but not the adelic version with its archimedean factor. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The archimedean discriminant is only gestured at ('defined through the natural topological ring isomorphism … following ELMV §6.1'). The paper defines it exactly: D_∞ = vol(Λ_∞)^2. The item also omits Remark 2.5, which says D_∞, D_{p_1}, D_{p_2} are constant under (♠) and asserts D_∞ = 1. As printed, the definition gives π^2 for the unit disc (see the new issue below). Same in arXiv v3 and print.

items.name: The global order Λ
items.statement: Define Λ := ∩_{v≠∞} Λ_v, the intersection taken in the 2-dimensional Q-vector space E(Q). It is a finite-index Z-sublattice of O_E closed under multiplication, hence an order in E, with discriminant ∏_{v≠∞} D_v; in general Λ ≠ E(Q) ∩ O. For every finite v, K_{T̃,v} := g_vO_v^×g_v^{-1} ∩ T̃(Q_v) equals Λ_v^×.
items.locator: §2.4.4, Definition 2.6 and Remark 2.7, pp. 166–167 (arXiv v3: Definition 10)
items.note: The global order attached to a homogeneous toral set, of which Pic(Λ) acts on the packet. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor, inherited from a misprint in Remark 2.7 (new issue below): the group equal to Λ_v^× is g_vO_v^×g_v^{-1} ∩ T̃(Q_v). With the order O_v in place of O_v^×, as printed and as in the item, the intersection is the monoid Λ_v ∩ E_v^×.

items.name: From ideles to ideals
items.statement: Let [T(A)g] be a homogeneous toral set with splitting field E/Q and global order Λ = ∩_{v≠∞}Λ_v ⊆ O_E. (1) 𝒥(Λ) (arXiv: Ideals(Λ)) is the group of invertible proper fractional Λ-ideals, which are exactly the locally principal fractional Λ-ideals. The map ĩdl : T̃(A_f)/K_{T̃,f} = ∏_{v≠∞}E_v^×/∏_{v≠∞}Λ_v^× → 𝒥(Λ), (α_vΛ_v^×)_v ↦ ∩_{v≠∞} α_vΛ_v ⊂ E, is a group isomorphism. (2) 𝒥(Λ)_0 := 𝒥(Λ) ∪ {0·Λ}. It carries a natural action of 𝒥(Λ), hence of the finite E-ideles, and ĩdl extends to a surjective equivariant map E(A_f)/K_{T̃,f} = ∏_{v≠∞}E_v/∏_{v≠∞}Λ_v^× → 𝒥(Λ)_0. This map is not a bijection: the preimage of 0·Λ contains every non-invertible adele, while each invertible ideal has exactly one preimage. (3) ĩdl descends to idl : T(A_f)/K_{T,f} = Q^×\∏_{v≠∞}E_v^×/∏_{v≠∞}Λ_v^× → Q^×\𝒥(Λ), the equality A_f^×\(…) = Q^×\(…) holding because Q has class number one.
items.locator: §2.4.4, Definition 2.8, p. 167 (print writes 𝒥(Λ) for arXiv's Ideals(Λ)) (arXiv v3: Definition 12)
items.note: The dictionary between the adelic twist s ∈ T(A) and an ideal class, which converts the dynamical statement into the arithmetic quantity 𝔑. The Tau Ceti orders layer constructs invertible proper fractional ideals and Pic(O) and warns that not every proper ideal is invertible; the idelic description is HE.0's territory. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Wrong definition of Ideals(Λ)_0. The item calls it 'the integral ones', but the paper defines 𝒥(Λ)_0 := 𝒥(Λ) ∪ {0·Λ}, the invertible ideals together with the zero ideal, a set with a 𝒥(Λ)-action that is the target of the extension of ĩdl to all finite adeles. Integrality is always imposed separately (e.g. '𝔞 ∈ 𝒥(Λ)_0, 𝔞 ⊆ Λ, … or 𝔞 = 0' in Definition 8.6, arXiv Definition 85). The item also drops the extended map on E(A_f)/K_{T̃,f}. Same in arXiv v3 and print. Review note on status: Plausibly planned in part. HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.0 plans 'proper invertible ideals, Pic(O_c), … and their comparison with the relevant idele-class quotients', and GlobalNumberFields layer 11 plans the invertible proper fractional ideals and Pic O. That is the idelic description in (1) and (3) for quadratic orders; the zero-extended map (2) is not planned.

items.name: Joinings of periodic toral measures
items.statement: For a maximal torus T < G anisotropic over Q, s ∈ T(A) and g ∈ G(A), the set [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] ⊂ [(G × G)(A)] is a joint homogeneous toral set, a homogeneous set for the non-maximal rank-one anisotropic torus T^Δ. It carries a probability measure μ^joint invariant under the right action of H_A^Δ, where H_A = g^{-1}T(A)g. Each coordinate projection of μ^joint is the periodic toral measure on [T(A)g], so μ^joint is a self-joining of it, the self-joining with twist s. The whole class of s in T(Q)\T(A) gives the same joining.
items.locator: §2.5, pp. 168–169 (joint packets §2.5.1, volume and discriminant §2.5.2, p. 169) (arXiv v3: Section 2.5)
items.note: The object the main theorem classifies. It is a joining in the sense of ergodic theory, and the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss classification of joinings is one of the inputs. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. The probability measure on [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] is invariant under H_A^Δ = (g^{-1}T(A)g)^Δ acting on the right (s commutes with T(A)); 'the T^Δ(A)-invariant probability measure' is loose in the same way as in item 9.

items.name: The residual quotient G_res
items.statement: Set G_res = G(Q)\G(A)/G(A)^+ and let π^+ : [G(A)] → G_res be the quotient map. The topological space G_res is a compact abelian group and the composite G(A) → [G(A)] → G_res is a continuous surjective group homomorphism.
items.locator: §3, Definition 3.1, p. 169 (arXiv v3: Definition 13)
items.note: The finite abelian quotient through which the connected components of the arithmetic quotient, and the residual spectrum, are seen. AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 plans strong approximation and the level maps that make this quotient finite, but not the quotient itself as a group with its induced measures.

items.name: Classification of limits of joinings of periodic toral measures
items.statement: Let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q, K_∞ < G(R) a maximal compact torus and p_1, p_2 finite primes. For each i let H_i = [T_i^Δ(A)(g_i, s_ig_i)] be a joint homogeneous toral set, with T_i < G a maximal torus defined and anisotropic over Q, g_i ∈ G(A) and s_i ∈ T_i(A). Let E_i be the quadratic field splitting T_i, D_i the discriminant of H_i, f_i the conductor (printed: f_i^2 is the largest square dividing D_i; the intended meaning is the conductor of the order Λ_i), and μ_i the algebraic probability measure on [(G × G)(A)] supported on H_i. Assume for all i: (1) g_{i,∞}^{-1}T_i(R)g_{i,∞} = K_∞; (2) p_1 and p_2 split in E_i; (3) the Dedekind zeta function of E_i has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero; (4) f_i ≪ 1. If |D_i| → ∞ and for every compact B ⊂ G(A) one has g_i^{-1}T_i(Q)s_ig_i ∩ B = ∅ for all i ≫_B 1, then every weak-* limit point of {μ_i} is a (G × G)(A)^+-invariant probability measure, hence a convex combination of the Haar measures on the fibres of π^+ × π^+. (For sets satisfying (♠), Proposition 7.8 shows the genericity condition is equivalent to min{Nr 𝔞 : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ_i invertible, [𝔞] = [idl(s_{i,f})] ∈ Pic(Λ_i)} → ∞.)
items.locator: §3.1, Theorem 3.2, pp. 169–170 (arXiv v3: Theorem 14)
items.note: The main adelic theorem, of which Theorem 3 is the geometric shadow. Together with the residual-spectrum proposition it describes the limit points completely. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Hypotheses misstated. The paper assumes (1) g_∞^{-1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞, (2) p_1, p_2 split in E_i, (3) no Landau–Siegel zero, (4) bounded conductor f_i ≪ 1, together with |D_i| → ∞ and the genericity condition 'for every compact B ⊂ G(A), g^{-1}T(Q)sg ∩ B = ∅ for i ≫_B 1'. The item drops the archimedean condition (1) and the bounded-conductor condition (4), which is essential and is the reason Theorem 1.3 assumes fundamental discriminants (see §1.8.2). It also replaces the genericity condition by '𝔑_i → ∞', which is equivalent only by Proposition 7.8 (arXiv Prop. 79). Same in arXiv v3 and print.

items.name: Equidistribution against the non-residual spectrum
items.statement: In the setting of the main adelic theorem, for every continuous compactly supported f in the orthogonal complement of the residual spectrum in L²([(G × G)(A)]) one has ∫ f dμ_i → 0.
items.locator: §3.1, Corollary 3.3, pp. 170–171 (arXiv v3: Corollary 15)
items.note: The functional form of the main theorem: all the surviving mass is residual.

items.name: Reduction to a fixed invariance group at p_1 and p_2
items.statement: Let {H_i} and {μ_i} be as in the main adelic theorem. Then there is a bounded sequence h_i ∈ G(A) such that H_i(h_i, h_i) ⊆ [(G × G)(A)] satisfies the normalisation conditions at p_1 and p_2; consequently the main theorem for joint homogeneous toral sets satisfying those conditions implies the general case.
items.locator: §3.2, Proposition 3.4 and Corollary 3.5, pp. 171–172 ('the normalisation conditions' are (♠)) (arXiv v3: Proposition 16 with Corollary 17)
items.note: The normalisation that lets the whole argument be run with a fixed compact-open invariance group at the two split primes.

items.name: Limit behaviour of the residual spectrum
items.statement: Let {μ_i} and E_i/Q be as in Theorem 3.2, without assuming its conditions (1)–(4). Assume that either the fields E_i are pairwise distinct, or all equal a fixed quadratic field E_0. Put H := G_res in the first case and H := ker(χ_{E_0} ∘ Nrd) < G_res in the second, where Nrd : G_res → Q^×\A^×/A^{×2} is the reduced-norm monomorphism and χ_{E_0} : Q^×\A^×/A^{×2} → {±1} is the quadratic character of E_0/Q given by class field theory. Then every weak-* limit point of (π^+ × π^+)_*μ_i is an H^Δ-invariant probability measure supported on a single coset of H^Δ. In general, even under these assumptions, (π^+ × π^+)_*μ_i need not converge.
items.locator: §3.3, Proposition 3.6 and Remark 3.7, pp. 172–173 (arXiv v3: Proposition 18)
items.note: This proposition computes exactly which convex combinations occur in the main theorem, and hence which connected components of Y × Y the joint packets can miss. It is a statement about the residual spectrum of the adelic quotient and about the distribution of the classes of the fields E_i. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Wrong conclusion. The item says the pushforwards 'converge to the Haar measure on the corresponding coset of H^Δ' and then says they need not converge. The paper proves that every limit point of (π^+ × π^+)_*μ_i is an H^Δ-invariant probability measure supported on a single coset of H^Δ; Remark 3.7 adds that the sequence need not converge. The item also leaves H unspecified in the second case: H = ker(χ_{E_0} ∘ Nrd). Same in arXiv v3 and print.

items.name: n-fold joint homogeneous toral sets
items.statement: Fix n ∈ N, a maximal torus T < G defined and anisotropic over Q, its diagonal T^Δ < G^{×n}, elements s_1, …, s_{n−1} ∈ T(A) and g ∈ G(A). The set [T^Δ(A)(g, s_1g, …, s_{n−1}g)] ⊂ [G^{×n}(A)] is an n-joint homogeneous toral set.
items.locator: §3.4, Definition 3.8, p. 173 (arXiv v3: Definition 20)
items.note: The n-fold generalisation of the basic object.

items.name: The n-fold theorem
items.statement: Let G, K_∞, p_1, p_2 be as in Theorem 3.2 and n ∈ N. For each i let H_i = [T_i^Δ(A)(g_i, s_{i,1}g_i, …, s_{i,n−1}g_i)] be an n-joint homogeneous toral set, with E_i, D_i, f_i as in Theorem 3.2 and μ_i the algebraic probability measure on [G^{×n}(A)] supported on H_i. Assume for all i: g_{i,∞}^{-1}T_i(R)g_{i,∞} = K_∞; p_1 and p_2 split in E_i; ζ_{E_i} has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero; f_i ≪ 1. If |D_i| → ∞ and, for every compact B ⊂ G(A) and every pair of distinct s, s' ∈ {1, s_{i,1}, …, s_{i,n−1}}, one has g_i^{-1}T_i(Q)s^{-1}s'g_i ∩ B = ∅ for all i ≫_B 1, then every weak-* limit point of {μ_i} is a G^{×n}(A)^+-invariant probability measure. The deduction applies Theorem 3.2 to each pair of coordinates and then the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss joinings theorem [EL15a, Cor. 1.5].
items.locator: §3.4, Theorem 3.9, p. 174 (arXiv v3: Theorem 21)
items.note: The n-fold result, which is what feeds the theorem on Galois orbits of special points on a product of n Shimura curves. The Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss joining classification is an external input and is listed as a prerequisite. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: 'The same hypotheses as the main adelic theorem, applied to every pair of coordinates' inherits the misstated hypotheses of item 18: it omits the conditions g_∞^{-1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞ and f_i ≪ 1, and the genericity condition is on every quotient s^{-1}s' of distinct twists in {1, s_1, …, s_{n−1}}. The printed proof cites 'Theorem 9.7' (the two-variable sieve theorem) where Theorem 3.2 is meant (new issue below). Same in arXiv v3 and print.

items.name: Galois orbits of special points on a product of Shimura curves
items.statement: Let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q split over R and X a product of n quaternionic Shimura varieties relative to G. Let {x_i} be special points of X all of whose coordinates have CM by the same quadratic order Λ_i < E_i, of discriminant D_i < 0 and conductor f_i. Fix primes p_1, p_2 and assume for all i: (1) p_1 and p_2 split in E_i; (2) the Dedekind zeta function of E_i has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero; (3) f_i ≪ 1. Let ν_i be the normalised counting measure on the Galois orbit of x_i. If {x_i} has finite intersection with every proper special subvariety, then every weak-* limit of {ν_i} is a convex combination of the uniform probability measures on the connected components of X.
items.locator: §3.5, Theorem 3.10, pp. 174–175 (arXiv v3: Theorem 22)
items.note: The geometric theorem, deduced from the n-fold toral theorem by the reciprocity map of class field theory. ShimuraVarieties V4 plans the reciprocity formula at special points and CM.6 the reciprocity exports; the equidistribution statement is new. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Missing hypothesis: the paper assumes (3) f_i ≪ 1, bounded conductors. The item names the conductor f_i but never assumes it bounded. Same in arXiv v3 and print.

items.name: Algebraic measures on adelic quotients
items.statement: Let M be a linear algebraic group over Q. (1) Fix a finite set S of places containing ∞, a closed finite-index subgroup M < M(Q_S) and a lattice Γ < M. A probability measure ν on Γ\M is algebraic if there are a closed unimodular algebraic subgroup L < M defined and anisotropic over Q, a finite-index subgroup L < L(Q_S) and g_S ∈ M such that ν is the L-Haar probability measure on [Lg_S] ⊆ Γ\M. (2) A probability measure ν on [M(A)] is algebraic if there are a closed unimodular algebraic Q-subgroup L < M anisotropic over Q, a Q-isogeny L' → L and a closed finite-index subgroup L < Im[L'(A) → L(A)] such that ν is the L-Haar probability measure on an orbit [Lg] ⊂ [M(A)], g ∈ M(A). The datum is the M(Q)-orbit of (L, L' → L, L, Lg), with γ acting by conjugation and left translation.
items.locator: §4, Definition 4.1 and Remark 4.2, p. 176 (arXiv v3: Definition 23)
items.note: The class of measures the rigidity theorem produces. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans equidistribution and ergodic methods for homogeneous spaces but not the adelic algebraic measures or their classification. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. In the S-arithmetic definition, ν is the Haar measure of a finite-index subgroup L < L(Q_S) on a closed orbit [Lg_S], not the measure 'invariant under L' on an orbit of L(Q_S). The paper's Definition 4.1(2) says 'for some g ∈ G(A)' and Remark 4.2 says 'G(Q)-orbit' where M(A) and M(Q) are meant.

items.name: The split tori A_{p_i} and their positive parts
items.statement: For i ∈ {1, 2}, A_{p_i} < G(Q_{p_i}) is the maximal split torus fixed once and for all in §2.4.1, with A_{p_1} ∩ K_{p_1} maximal compact in A_{p_1}; every homogeneous toral set considered satisfies g_{p_i}^{-1}T(Q_{p_i})g_{p_i} = A_{p_i} by (♠). Put A_{p_i}^+ := A_{p_i} ∩ G(Q_{p_i})^+, the image in A_{p_i} of a maximal torus of G^sc(Q_{p_i}) isogenous to A_{p_i}; it has finite index in A_{p_i}.
items.locator: §4, Definition 4.3, p. 176 (A_{p_i} fixed in §2.4.1 'Special places', p. 163) (arXiv v3: Definition 25)
items.note: The diagonal flow whose invariance the rigidity theorem produces. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: A_{p_i} is misdescribed as 'the maximal split torus determined by the splitting of E at p_i'. It is fixed once and for all, independently of E, with A_{p_1} ∩ K_{p_1} maximal compact in A_{p_1}; the tori T are moved onto it by (♠).

items.name: Measure rigidity for limits of toral joinings
items.statement: Let μ_i^joint be self-joinings of periodic toral measures on [(G × G)(A)] whose toral sets satisfy (♠), with |D_i| → ∞, and let μ be a weak-* limit point. Then μ is a convex combination of (A_{p_1}^+ × A_{p_2}^+)^Δ-invariant algebraic measures: there is a Borel probability measure P on M_1([(G × G)(A)]), supported on algebraic measures, with μ = ∫ λ dP(λ). For P-almost every λ the associated Q-group L < G × G can be taken to be G^Δ or G × G, and λ is the algebraic measure on [L(A)^+ξ] for some ξ ∈ (G × G)(A). For L = G × G this is the Haar measure on a fibre of π^+ × π^+.
items.locator: §4, Theorem 4.4, p. 176 (arXiv v3: Theorem 26)
items.note: The rigidity half of the proof, deduced from the classification of joinings of Einsiedler and Lindenstrauss together with Linnik's basic lemma and the equidistribution of the torus orbits in each coordinate. This is the statement closest to GN.4's plan for ergodic methods in Duke-type applications, and it is what the cross-correlation estimate is then used to rule out. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. The hypothesis is (♠), which includes the archimedean condition g_∞^{-1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞ as well as the conditions at p_1 and p_2. The dichotomy holds for P-almost every λ, not for each λ, and it is stated through the Q-group L ∈ {G^Δ, G × G}.

items.name: Restriction on the Hecke parameter of a limit
items.statement: If λ is an algebraic measure in the support of P and is supported on [G^Δ(A)^+ξ], then ctr(ξ)_{p_i} ∈ A_{p_i} for i ∈ {1,2}.
items.locator: §4, Corollary 4.5, p. 177 (arXiv v3: Corollary 27)
items.note: The constraint at the two split primes on the surviving Hecke correspondences.

items.name: Mixing of G(Q_v)^+ on the simply connected adelic quotient
items.statement: For every rational place v that splits B, the action of G(Q_v)^+ is mixing for the Haar measure on [G(A)^+ω_0], for every ω_0 ∈ G(A).
items.locator: §4, Lemma 4.6, p. 177 (arXiv v3: Lemma 28)
items.note: The mixing input to the ergodic decomposition. GN.4 plans ergodic and mixing proofs for homogeneous spaces; the adelic statement with the simply connected subgroup is the form needed here. Review note on status: Stays missing. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4 schedules 'ergodic/mixing' proofs for Duke-type applications, but neither Howe–Moore nor the adelic statement for G^sc is named.

items.name: Ergodic decomposition of a limit joining
items.statement: For P-almost every λ there is ω = (ω_1, ω_2) ∈ G(A) × G(A) such that λ is an (A_{p_1}^+ × A_{p_2}^+)^Δ-invariant measure supported on [(G × G)(A)^+ω], whose projection to each coordinate is the G(A)^+-Haar measure on the corresponding orbit.
items.locator: §4, Lemma 4.7, p. 178 (arXiv v3: Lemma 29)
items.note: The reduction of the classification to genuine joinings of Haar measures.

items.name: Reduction to an S-arithmetic joining
items.statement: Let λ satisfy the conclusions of Lemma 4.7, so that λ is supported on [G(A)^+ω_1 × G(A)^+ω_2]. Let S be a finite set of places with ∞, p_1, p_2 ∈ S, such that G has class number one with respect to K^S and ω_1, ω_2 ∈ G(Q_S) × K^S. Let ⅁^S : [(G × G)(A)] → Y_S × Y_S := Γ_S\G(Q_S) × Γ_S\G(Q_S), Γ_S := G(Q) ∩ K^S, be the canonical projection. Then ⅁^S_*λ is an algebraic measure on Y_S × Y_S supported on [L_Sg_S] for some g_S ∈ (G × G)(Q_S), where L < G × G is a closed algebraic Q-subgroup and L_S < L(Q_S) ∩ (G × G)(Q_S)^+ has finite index. L is isogenous to G or to G × G and projects onto G in both coordinates.
items.locator: §4, Lemma 4.8, pp. 178–179 (arXiv v3: Lemma 30)
items.note: The step that makes the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss joining classification applicable. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor, incomplete. The conclusion of the lemma is about the projection ⅁^S_*λ to Y_S × Y_S = Γ_S\G(Q_S) × Γ_S\G(Q_S), with Γ_S = G(Q) ∩ K^S. That projection is supported on [L_Sg_S], where L_S has finite index in L(Q_S) ∩ (G × G)(Q_S)^+, and L is isogenous to G or to G × G and projects onto G in both coordinates. Lemma 4.9 (item 32) needs this last part. The print has 'L < G' for L < G × G (new issue below).

items.name: The isomorphism type of the joining subgroup
items.statement: In the previous setting the group L is isomorphic either to G or to G × G; and if L < G × G is isomorphic to G and projects onto G in both coordinates then it is conjugate to G^Δ over Q. Moreover one may take L_S = L(Q_S)^+.
items.locator: §4, Lemmas 4.9, 4.10 and 4.11, pp. 179–180 (arXiv v3: Lemmas 31, 32 and 33)
items.note: The dichotomy between the trivial joining, which is the Haar measure, and a graph joining supported on a Hecke correspondence. Ruling out the second is exactly what the cross-correlation bound does.

items.name: Coordinates for a quaternion algebra split by E
items.statement: M_{2×2} = Spec Q[x_{i,j} : 1 ≤ i, j ≤ 2]. GL_2 is the closed subscheme of M_{2×2} × A^1 with Q[GL_2] = Q[x_{i,j}, det^{-1}]/⟨(x_{1,1}x_{2,2} − x_{1,2}x_{2,1})det^{-1} = 1⟩. Let Ã < GL_2 be the diagonal torus. Since T̃ ≅ Res_{E/Q}G_m splits over E, fix an E-algebra isomorphism B_E → M_{2×2,E} carrying T̃_E to Ã_E, and identify B_E = M_{2×2,E}, B_E^× = GL_{2,E}, T̃_E = Ã_E, G_E = PGL_{2,E}, T_E = A_E. With 𝔊 = Gal(E/Q) = {1, σ}, the naive action of σ is x_{i,j} ↦ ^σx_{i,j}, and the twisted action giving the Q-form B is x ↦ θ·^σx·θ^{-1} for some θ ∈ PGL_2(E). The two actions differ even when B = M_{2×2}.
items.locator: §5, Definitions 5.1 and 5.2, p. 182 (arXiv v3: Definitions 34 and 35)
items.note: The explicit coordinates in which every local computation of the paper is carried out. The Tau Ceti quadratic-form roadmap constructs quaternion algebras and their splitting criterion; this Galois-descent presentation relative to a fixed maximal subfield and a fixed torus is the paper's own set-up. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. The coordinate ring of GL_2 is the quotient Q[x_{i,j}, det^{-1}]/((x_{1,1}x_{2,2} − x_{1,2}x_{2,1})det^{-1} − 1), not Q[x_{i,j}, det^{-1}], which is the ring of M_{2×2} × A^1. The print contains E3 ('identity' for 'identify') at this point.

items.name: Normal form of the twisting element
items.statement: The twisting element θ has a representative of the form θ = ((0, ε), (1, 0)) with ε ∈ Q^×; every ε ∈ Q^× defines in this way an inner form of M_{2×2} split over E, and the inner forms attached to ε_1, ε_2 are isomorphic over Q if and only if ε_1/ε_2 ∈ Nr(E^×).
items.locator: §5, Proposition 5.3, p. 183 (print writes 'ε_2 ∈ ε_1 Nrd E^×' where the field norm Nr is meant) (arXiv v3: Proposition 36)
items.note: The classification of the forms in these coordinates, by the norm class of ε. Review note on status: Partly planned: QuadraticFormInvariants layer 2 plans ℍ[K,a,b], the symbol relations and the norm criterion for splitting, and the classification of (E, ε) by ε mod Nr(E^×) follows from the Brauer-group bilinearity of layer 7. The item as stated is not named anywhere, so missing is defensible.

items.name: Rational and local points in coordinates
items.statement: B(Q) = {((a, εb), (^σb, ^σa)) : a, b ∈ E} inside M_{2×2}(E), and likewise B(Q_v) = {((α, εβ), (^σβ, ^σα)) : α, β ∈ E_v} inside M_{2×2}(E_v), the rational points being the matrices with entries in E.
items.locator: §5, Proposition 5.5, p. 183, and §5.1, Proposition 5.6, p. 184 (arXiv v3: Propositions 38 and 39)
items.note: The explicit description of the points of the form, used in every subsequent computation.

items.name: The different ideal of a local order
items.statement: For v ≠ ∞ define the inverse different of Λ_v ⊂ E_v by Λ̂_v = {a ∈ E_v : Tr(aΛ_v) ⊆ Z_v} and the different by 𝔇(Λ_v) = (Λ_v : Λ̂_v) = {a ∈ Λ_v : aΛ̂_v ⊆ Λ_v}.
items.locator: §5.2, Definition 5.7, p. 184 (arXiv v3: Definition 40)
items.note: The different of a local quadratic order. The Tau Ceti algebraic-curves roadmap constructs the different for a function field extension and the global number fields roadmap the different of the maximal order; the different of a non-maximal local order, with its relation to the discriminant, is what is needed here.

items.name: The different is principal with norm the discriminant
items.statement: For v ≠ ∞ the different 𝔇(Λ_v) is principal and invertible, and its generator 𝒟_v ∈ Λ_v, well defined up to a unit of Λ_v, satisfies Nr 𝒟_v = D_v.
items.locator: §5.2, Lemma 5.8 with Remark 5.9, p. 184 (arXiv v3: Lemma 41)
items.note: The identity that converts the discriminant into an explicit element of the order, used throughout Section 4.

items.name: Local maximal orders at split places
items.statement: Let v ≠ ∞ with B(Q_v) split, write ε = f·^σf with f ∈ E_v^×, and identify B(Q_v) with End_{Q_v}(E_v) as in Lemma 5.10. Then End_{Z_v}(Λ_v) = {((α, βf), (^σβ/f, ^σα)) : α ∈ Λ̂_v, β − ^σα ∈ Λ_v}. There is τ_v ∈ E_v^× (namely τ_v = (l/^σl)·f, where g_vO_vg_v^{-1} = End_{Z_v}(lΛ_v) with l ∈ E_v^×) such that g_vO_vg_v^{-1} = {((α, βτ_v), (^σβ/τ_v, ^σα)) : α ∈ Λ̂_v, β − ^σα ∈ Λ_v}. Given α ∈ Λ̂_v, the condition β − ^σα ∈ Λ_v is equivalent to α + β ∈ Λ_v. For almost all v, τ_v ∈ Λ_v^×.
items.locator: §5.3.1, Lemma 5.11, Proposition 5.12 with Remark 5.13, and Proposition 5.14, pp. 185–186 (arXiv v3: Lemma 44 with Propositions 45 and 47)
items.note: The explicit local description of the conjugated maximal order in the chosen coordinates; it is what makes the invariants of Section 7 computable as ideals. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. f is not introduced: it is an element of E_v^× with ε = f·^σf, which exists because B(Q_v) is split. End_{Z_v}(Λ_v) is taken through the identification B(Q_v) ≅ End_{Q_v}(E_v) of Lemma 5.10, which no item states (see coverage). Proposition 5.12 is printed with only 'v ≠ ∞' but sits in the split subsection §5.3.1 and uses Lemma 5.10, so B(Q_v) split is a hypothesis, as the item correctly has it.

items.name: The archimedean analogue
items.statement: Assume B(R) is split and write ε = f·^σf, f ∈ C^×. For α, β ∈ C, ‖g_∞^{-1}((α, βf), (^σβ/f, ^σα))g_∞‖_∞ = |α| + |β|. Hence g_∞Ω̃_∞g_∞^{-1} = {((α, βf), (^σβ/f, ^σα)) : α, β ∈ C, |α| + |β| ≤ 2, |α| − |β| ≥ 1/2} and g_∞O_∞g_∞^{-1} = {((α, βf), (^σβ/f, ^σα)) : α, β ∈ C, |α| + |β| ≤ 1}.
items.locator: §5.3.1, Proposition 5.15, p. 187 (arXiv v3: Proposition 48)
items.note: The archimedean counterpart of the local description, which makes the archimedean orbital integral computable. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Imprecise. The item does not state the two sets the proposition computes, and it omits that the statement lives in the split case (B(R) ≅ M_2(R), ε = f·^σf with f ∈ C^×).

items.name: Local maximal orders at ramified places
items.statement: (a) Let v be inert in E with B(Q_v) ramified, π a uniformiser of Z_v, and ε = π^{2k+1}u with k ∈ Z, u ∈ Z_v^×. Then Λ_v = Λ̂_v = O_{E_v} and g_vO_vg_v^{-1} = O_v = {((α, π^{k+1}uβ), (π^{-k}·^σβ, ^σα)) : α, β ∈ Λ_v}. (b) Let E_v/Q_v and B(Q_v) both be ramified and Π a uniformiser of O_{E_v}. Then ε = Nr(Π)^k·u with k ∈ Z and u ∈ Z_v^× not a norm from E_v^×, and g_vO_vg_v^{-1} ⊆ {((α, Π^kuβ), (Π^{-k}·^σβ, ^σα)) : α, β ∈ Λ̂_v}. (c) Hence for every finite v there are τ_v ∈ E_v^× and υ_v ∈ Q_v^× with υ_v·Nr(τ_v) = ε such that g_vO_vg_v^{-1} ⊆ {((α, βυ_vτ_v), (^σβ/τ_v, ^σα)) : α, β ∈ Λ̂_v}. Here υ_v = 1 if B splits at v; υ_v = πu, a uniformiser, and τ_v = π^k if B ramifies and E is inert at v; υ_v = u, a unit that is not a norm, and τ_v = Π^k if both ramify. τ_v ∈ Λ_v^× for almost all v, and τ_v = 1 at every ramified place of B once ε is chosen within ε·Nr(E^×) (Prop. 5.3) with ord_v ε = 1 at the ramified places of B inert in E and ord_v ε = 0 at those ramified in E.
items.locator: §5.3.2–5.3.3, Propositions 5.17, 5.18 and 5.19, pp. 188–189 (Lemma 5.16, p. 188, is item 92) (arXiv v3: Propositions 50, 51 and 52)
items.note: The ramified cases of the local description, needed because the quaternion algebra is an arbitrary form. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Inherits a slip of the paper (new issue below). With ord_v ε = 2k + 1 and ε = π^{2k+1}u (u ∈ Z_v^×), the proof of Prop. 5.17 gives the (1,2) entry επ^{-k}β = π^{k+1}uβ, but the statement prints π^{k+1}β. That is correct only when ε = π^{2k+1} for the chosen uniformiser. The item's summary of Prop. 5.19 gives the value of υ_v only in the split case. The paper's further claim 'τ_v = 1 if B is ramified at v' holds only after ε is normalised at the ramified places; in general Props. 5.17–5.18 give τ_v = π^k and τ_v = Π^k. Same in arXiv v3 and print.

items.name: Denominators and good integral representatives
items.statement: (1) For finite v where G splits, ℬ_v is the Bruhat–Tits tree of G(Q_v); for finite v where G ramifies, ℬ_v is the connected graph with two vertices G(Q_v)/K_v; d is the path metric with edges of length 1. (2) If B(R) is split, ℬ_∞ = G(R)/N_{G(R)}(K_∞), the upper half-plane with the standard hyperbolic distance d; if B(R) is ramified, ℬ_∞ is a point. (3) For each place v let x_0 ∈ ℬ_v be the point fixed by K_v, let q be the residue characteristic if v ≠ ∞ and q = e if v = ∞, and define the continuous function 𝔡_v : G(Q_v) → R_{>0} (arXiv: Denom_v) by 𝔡_v(x_v) := q^{d(x_0, x_v.x_0)}. (4) 𝔡_f : G(A_f) → N is the continuous function 𝔡_f((x_v)_{v≠∞}) := ∏_{v≠∞} 𝔡_v(x_v).
items.locator: §5.4, Definition 5.20, p. 189 (print writes 𝔡_v, 𝔡_f for arXiv's Denom_v, Denom_f) (arXiv v3: Definition 53)
items.note: The complexity function on the Hecke correspondences, whose size controls the volume of a homogeneous Hecke set. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Wrong at the archimedean place, and vague elsewhere. The paper defines 𝔡_∞(x) = e^{d(x_0, x.x_0)} with d the hyperbolic distance on the upper half-plane G(R)/N_{G(R)}(K_∞), with 𝔡_∞ ≡ 1 if B(R) is ramified. It is not 'defined by the operator norm'. At finite v the denominator is exactly q^{d(x_0, x_v.x_0)}, not merely something that 'measures the distance'. Same in arXiv v3 and print. Review note on status: Partly planned: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 plans the SL_2 tree and its lattice model. The denominator function is not planned.

items.name: Good integral representatives
items.statement: (a) Let v be a place and x_v ∈ G(Q_v). For every h ∈ Ω_vx_vΩ_v there is r ∈ O_v ⊂ B(Q_v) with h = Z(Q_v)r and |Nrd r|_v·𝔡_v(x_v) = 1 if v ≠ ∞, 2^{-8} ≤ |Nrd r|_∞·𝔡_∞(x_∞) ≤ 1 if v = ∞. For v ≠ ∞ this r is optimal: no representative of h in O_v has reduced norm of smaller valuation. (b) Fix ξ_{p_1} ∈ A_{p_1} and n ≥ 0. For every h ∈ K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)}ξ_{p_1}K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)} there is r ∈ O_{p_1}^{(−n,n)} := ∩_{k=−n}^{n} a^kO_{p_1}a^{-k} with h = Z(Q_{p_1})r and |Nrd r|_{p_1}·𝔡_{p_1}(ξ_{p_1}) = 1.
items.locator: §5.4, Propositions 5.21 and 5.23, pp. 190–191 (arXiv v3: Proposition 54 with Proposition 56)
items.note: The normalisation of representatives of a Hecke element by an integral quaternion of controlled reduced norm; it is what turns the counting problem into a count of integral ideals. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The Bowen-ball clause drops its hypotheses and conclusion. Prop. 5.23 holds for ξ_{p_1} ∈ A_{p_1} (not arbitrary x_{p_1}), for h ∈ K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)}ξ_{p_1}K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)}, and it gives a representative r in O_{p_1}^{(−n,n)} = ∩_{|k|≤n} a^kO_{p_1}a^{-k}, not merely in O_{p_1}. The item also omits the optimality clause of Prop. 5.21. Same in arXiv v3 and print.

items.name: Bowen balls for the diagonal flow
items.statement: Let B ⊆ G(Q_{p_1}) be an identity neighbourhood, λ a cocharacter spanning X_•(A_{p_1}) and a = λ(p_1). The symmetric homogeneous B-Bowen ball is B^{(−n,n)} = ∩_{k=−n}^{n} a^kBa^{-k}.
items.locator: §5.4, Definition 5.22, p. 190 (arXiv v3: Definition 55)
items.note: The shrinking neighbourhoods along the diagonal flow in which the correlation is measured.

items.name: The GIT double quotient W
items.statement: Let M = G × T act on the affine variety G × G, the G-coordinate by diagonal left multiplication and the T-coordinate by diagonal right multiplication by the inverse; W denotes the GIT quotient G^Δ\(G × G)/T^Δ. Let w_T ∈ N_G T(Q) be a rational representative of the nontrivial Weyl class; the variety w_TT is well defined even though w_T is not.
items.locator: §6.1, Definitions 6.1 and 6.2, p. 191 (arXiv v3: Definitions 57 and 58)
items.note: The invariant-theoretic quotient whose points index the terms of the geometric expansion of the cross-correlation.

items.name: Orbits and stabilisers in the double quotient
items.statement: Let γ = (γ_1, γ_2) ∈ (G × G)(Q). (1) The M-orbit of γ is Zariski closed. (2) If ctr(γ) = γ_1^{-1}γ_2 ∉ N_GT(Q), the stabiliser M_γ is trivial. If ctr(γ) ∈ N_GT(Q), then t ↦ (γ_1tγ_1^{-1}, t) is an isomorphism Z_T(ctr γ) → M_γ, where Z_T(ctr γ) = T if ctr(γ) ∈ T(Q) and Z_T(ctr γ) = T[2] if ctr(γ) ∈ w_TT(Q); T[2] ≅ μ_2 over Q. (3) If ctr(γ) ∉ w_TT(Q), then ker[H^1(Q, M_γ) → H^1(Q, M)] is a singleton. (4) If ctr(γ) ∉ w_TT(Q), then π_W^{-1}(π_W(γ))(Q) is a single M(Q)-orbit.
items.locator: §6.1, Proposition 6.3, pp. 191–193 (arXiv v3: Proposition 59)
items.note: The orbit-stabiliser analysis that separates the terms of the geometric expansion into those with compact and non-compact stabilisers. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Incomplete. The item states only parts (1)–(2). It omits part (3), that ker[H^1(Q, M_γ) → H^1(Q, M)] is trivial when ctr(γ) ∉ w_TT(Q), and part (4), that the rational points of the π_W-fibre through γ form a single M(Q)-orbit. Part (4) is what Corollary 6.5 (item 46) and Lemma 7.3 (item 52) use. It also omits the explicit isomorphism and T[2] ≅ μ_2. The print writes π_W^{-1}(γ)(Q) for the fibre π_W^{-1}(π_W(γ))(Q).

items.name: The adjoint quotient of G by T and rational separation
items.statement: The natural morphism W → Ad T\G is an isomorphism. Moreover, writing π_W^0 : G → Ad T\G ≅ W for the Ad T-equivariant projection, for γ_0 ∈ G(Q) with γ_0 ∉ w_TT(Q) the rational fibre (π_W^0)^{-1}(γ_0)(Q) is a single Ad T(Q)-orbit.
items.locator: §6.2, Proposition 6.4 and Corollary 6.5, p. 194 (arXiv v3: Proposition 60 with Corollary 61)
items.note: The identification of the double quotient with an adjoint quotient, which makes it computable, together with the rational separation statement that makes each term of the geometric expansion a single rational orbit.

items.name: The simply connected torus T^{(1)}
items.statement: G^sc is the group of unit quaternions in B; T^{(1)} is the maximal torus of G^sc over Q mapping to T under the isogeny, namely the unit quaternions in T̃. Likewise A^{(1)} < GL_2 is the rank-one torus of diagonal matrices of determinant 1 and A the split diagonal torus of PGL_2, with A^{(1)} → A surjective as schemes.
items.locator: §6.2, Definition 6.6, p. 194, and §6.3, Definition 6.7, p. 195 (arXiv v3: Definitions 62 and 63)
items.note: The simply connected tori through which the invariant theory is computed.

items.name: The invariant functions ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ
items.statement: Let A^{(1)} act on M_{2×2} × A^1 by conjugating the matrix and fixing the det^{-1} coordinate; this is equivariant for GL_2 ↪ M_{2×2} × A^1. Define ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ ∈ Q[M_{2×2}] to be, respectively, the two diagonal entries and the product of the off-diagonal entries.
items.locator: §6.3, Definition 6.8, p. 195 (arXiv v3: Definition 64)
items.note: The explicit generators of the invariant ring.

items.name: The invariant rings
items.statement: Q[M_{2×2} × A^1]^{Ad A^{(1)}} = Q[ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ, det^{-1}], a polynomial algebra; Q[GL_2]^{Ad A^{(1)}} is its quotient by the relation (ϑ_1ϑ_2 − ψ)det^{-1} = 1; and with the grading in which ϑ_1, ϑ_2 have degree 1, ψ degree 2 and det^{-1} degree −2, the ring of Ad A-invariants on PGL_2 is the degree-zero part of the same quotient, generated by ψ det^{-1}, ϑ_1²det^{-1} and ϑ_2²det^{-1}, and isomorphic to Q[x, y, z]/(x² = yz).
items.locator: §6.3, Lemma 6.9, Proposition 6.10, Definition 6.11, Corollary 6.12 and Remark 6.13, pp. 195–196 (the item's form of Remark 6.13 is the correct one; the print has a misprint, see the new issue below) (arXiv v3: Lemma 65 with Propositions 66, 67 and Corollary 68)
items.note: The explicit computation of the invariant ring of the adjoint action of the diagonal torus on PGL_2, which is the local model for the GIT double quotient.

items.name: Galois behaviour of the invariants and descent
items.statement: For g ∈ B^×(Q) ⊂ GL_2(E), or g ∈ B^×(Q_v) ⊂ GL_2(E_v), one has ^σϑ_1(g) = ϑ_2(g), ^σψ(g) = ψ(g) and ^σdet^{-1}(g) = det^{-1}(g). Consequently the image of g ∈ G(Q) in W(Q) is determined by the two values ϑ_1²det^{-1}(g) and ψ det^{-1}(g) in E.
items.locator: §6.4, Lemma 6.14 and Proposition 6.15, p. 197 (arXiv v3: Lemma 70 with Proposition 71)
items.note: The descent of the invariant theory from the split form over E to the given Q-form; it is what makes the invariants of the geometric expansion rational.

items.name: Homogeneous Hecke sets
items.statement: For ξ = (ξ_1, ξ_2) ∈ (G × G)(A), [G^Δ(A)ξ] is a homogeneous Hecke set; it carries a ξ^{-1}G^Δ(A)ξ-invariant algebraic probability measure. [G^Δ(A)^+ξ] is a simply connected homogeneous Hecke set; it carries a ξ^{-1}G^Δ(A)^+ξ-invariant algebraic probability measure. With G^Δ fixed, [G^Δ(A)ξ] is determined by the coset G^Δ(A)ξ ∈ G^Δ(A)\(G × G)(A), identified through the contraction map with ctr(ξ) ∈ G(A). [G^Δ(A)^+ξ] is determined by G^Δ(A)^+ξ ∈ G^Δ(A)^+\(G × G)(A), identified with the pair ([ξ_1] ∈ G(A)/G(A)^+, ctr(ξ) ∈ G(A)).
items.locator: §7, Definition 7.1 and Remark 7.2, p. 197 (arXiv v3: Definition 72)
items.note: The Hecke correspondences on which the non-Haar limit measures would be supported; ruling them out is the content of the cross-correlation estimate. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Wrong datum. The paper's Remark 7.2 says that, with G^Δ fixed, [G^Δ(A)ξ] is determined by [ξ] ∈ G^Δ(A)\(G × G)(A), identified through ctr with ctr(ξ) ∈ G(A). The item's 'class of ξ in G^Δ(Q)\(G × G)(A)/G^Δ(A)' puts the groups on the wrong sides. It also omits the simply connected datum ([ξ_1] ∈ G(A)/G(A)^+, ctr(ξ)). The print's Definition 7.1 has 'ξG^Δ(A)^+ξ-invariant', a misprint for ξ^{-1}G^Δ(A)^+ξ (new issue below).

items.name: Hecke sets containing a joint toral set
items.statement: Every homogeneous Hecke set containing [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] is of the form [G^Δ(A)(g, t_Q sg)] for some t_Q ∈ T(Q).
items.locator: §7.1, Lemma 7.3, p. 198 (Remark 7.4, p. 198, is not in any item; see coverage) (arXiv v3: Lemma 74)
items.note: The parametrisation of the Hecke correspondences that could carry a limit measure.

items.name: The split-place denominator
items.statement: Define the proper continuous function Denom_sf : G(A_f) → N by Denom_sf(h_f) = ∏_{v ≠ ∞ splitting B} Denom_v(h_v); since 1 ≤ Denom_v(ξ_v) ≤ q_v at the finitely many ramified places, Denom_sf ≍_G Denom_f on G(A_f).
items.locator: §7.2.1, Definition 7.5, p. 199 (print: 𝔡_sf) (arXiv v3: Definition 76)
items.note: The multiplicative complexity that measures the volume of a Hecke correspondence.

items.name: Volume of a homogeneous Hecke set
items.statement: For ξ ∈ (G × G)(A) with ctr(ξ)_∞ ∈ K_∞ one has vol([G^Δ(A)ξ])·m_G(Ω) = Denom_sf(ctr(ξ)_f)·∏_{p | Denom_sf(ctr(ξ)_f)}(1 + 1/p).
items.locator: §7.2.1, Lemma 7.6, pp. 199–200 (arXiv v3: Lemma 77)
items.note: The exact volume of a Hecke correspondence in terms of its denominator; it is the quantity against which the packet's own volume must be compared, and it is why the method of Ellenberg, Michel and Venkatesh needs 𝔑 ≪ |D|^{1/2−η}.

items.name: The denominator is the minimal ideal norm
items.statement: For τ ∈ T(A) the denominator Denom_f(g_f^{-1}τ_fg_f) is the minimal norm of an integral fractional ideal in the homothety class idl(τ) ∈ Q^×\Ideals(Λ).
items.locator: §7.3, Lemma 7.7, p. 200 (print: 'integral fraction ideal' for 'integral fractional ideal'; 𝒥(Λ) for Ideals(Λ)) (arXiv v3: Lemma 78)
items.note: The arithmetic meaning of the denominator: it translates the dynamical complexity of the twist into the arithmetic quantity 𝔑 of the mixing conjecture.

items.name: Equivalence of the necessary conditions for equidistribution
items.statement: Let {[T_i^Δ(A)(g_i, s_ig_i)]}_i be a sequence of joint homogeneous toral sets with associated global orders Λ_i. Put 𝔰_i = idl(s_{i,f}) ∈ Q^×\𝒥(Λ_i), and let [𝔰_i] be its class in Pic(Λ_i). The following are equivalent. (1) min{vol([G^Δ(A)ξ]) : [G^Δ(A)ξ] ⊇ [T_i^Δ(A)(g_i,s_ig_i)]} → ∞ as i → ∞. (2) min{Nr 𝔞 : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ_i, [𝔞] = [𝔰_i]} → ∞ as i → ∞. (3) For every compact B ⊂ G(A) there is N ∈ N with g_i^{-1}T_i(Q)s_ig_i ∩ B = ∅ for all i > N.
items.locator: §7.3, Proposition 7.8, p. 201 (arXiv v3: Proposition 79)
items.note: The proof that the dynamical hypothesis and the arithmetic hypothesis 𝔑_i → ∞ of the mixing conjecture are the same condition, so that the theorem is stated in its natural generality. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Condition (3) is wrong and condition (1) is paraphrased inexactly. In print, as in v3, (1) says that the minimal VOLUME of a homogeneous Hecke set [G^Δ(A)ξ] containing the i-th joint toral set tends to ∞. The item says 'denominator'; the two agree only up to ∏_{p|N}(1+1/p) ≪ log log N, via Lemmas 7.3, 7.6 and 7.7. (2) is the minimal-norm condition. (3) is the non-concentration of the discrete orbit g_i^{-1}T_i(Q)s_ig_i: it eventually misses every compact set. The item's 'corresponding condition on 𝔑_i in the mixing conjecture' is condition (2), not (3). Both versions print '𝔞 ⊆ Λ' in (2) where Λ_i is meant (source issue). Print writes 𝔡_v, 𝔡_f and 𝒥(Λ), 𝒥(Λ)_0 where arXiv v3 writes Denom_v, Denom_f and Ideals(Λ), Ideals(Λ)_0; the corrected statements below use the printed notation.

items.name: The automorphic kernel and the pair cross-correlation
items.statement: For a compact identity neighbourhood V ⊆ [(G×G)(A)], the automorphic kernel K_V : [(G×G)(A)]^{×2} → R is K_V(x,y) = Σ_{γ∈(G×G)(Q)} 1_V(x^{-1}γy). The sum is finite, and the number of non-zero terms is bounded uniformly for x, y in fixed compact sets. Let B = ∏_v B_v ⊆ G(A) be a compact identity neighbourhood with B_v = K_v for almost all v and B_v a compact-open subgroup for every non-archimedean v. Let λ_1, λ_2 be probability measures on [(G×G)(A)] and C ⊆ [G(A)] closed. Define Cor_C[λ_1,λ_2](B) := ∫_{C×C}∫_{C×C} K_{B×B}(x,y) dλ_1(x) dλ_2(y), and Cor[λ_1,λ_2](B) := Cor_{Y_A}[λ_1,λ_2](B). B is injective on C if the quotient map G(A) → [G(A)] is injective on gB for every g with [g] ∈ C; for compact C such an identity neighbourhood exists. Then λ_1×λ_2({(x,y) ∈ (C×C)×(C×C) : y ∈ x(B×B)}) ≤ Cor_C[λ_1,λ_2](B), with equality if B is injective on C.
items.locator: §8.1, Definitions 8.1 and 8.2 and Lemma 8.3, pp. 201–202 (arXiv v3: Definitions 80 and 81 with Lemma 82)
items.note: The quantity the paper estimates: it measures how much a packet concentrates near a Hecke correspondence, and bounding it is what rules out the non-Haar limits left by the rigidity theorem. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. B_v must be a compact-open SUBGROUP at every non-archimedean v; the item says only 'compact open'. The injectivity notion used in Lemma 8.3 is not defined in the item. In Lemma 8.3 the set is {(x,y) ∈ (C×C)² : y ∈ x(B×B)}; print's 'y ∈ xB' is a harmless abuse.

items.name: The ideals attached to a joint toral set
items.statement: Fix a joint homogeneous toral set [T^Δ(A)(g,sg)] with global order Λ. (1) The twist s ∈ T(A) defines the homothety class Q^×𝔰 := idl(s) ∈ Q^×\𝒥(Λ) of invertible fractional Λ-ideals. (2) 𝔢 := idl~((υ_vτ_v)_v), where υ_v, τ_v are the local elements of Proposition 5.19 in the coordinates of the local maximal orders. It is an invertible fractional Λ-ideal recording the splitting of B outside ∞. (3) υ := sign(ε)·∏_{p : B is ramified at p and E is inert at p} p ∈ Z. When G ≃ PGL_2 is split, one may take ε = 1, and then υ = 1 and 𝔢 = Λ.
items.locator: §8.2, Definition 8.4 and Remark 8.5, p. 202 (arXiv v3: Definition 83 with Remark 84)
items.note: The arithmetic data entering the shifted-convolution sum. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The integer υ of Definition 8.4(3) is missing. It is part of the modulus υp_1^{2n} of the shifted convolution in Theorem 8.7. 𝔢 is defined from the local elements υ_v, τ_v of Proposition 5.19, not from ε.

items.name: The counting functions f_{[𝔤]} and g_{[𝔤]}
items.statement: For [𝔤] ∈ Pic(Λ) define f_{[𝔤]}, g_{[𝔤]} : Z → Z by g_{[𝔤]}(x) = #{𝔞 ∈ 𝒥(Λ)_0 : Nr 𝔞 = x, 𝔞 ⊆ Λ, and [𝔞] = [𝔤] or 𝔞 = 0} and f_{[𝔤]}(x) = #{𝔟 ∈ 𝒥(Λ) : Nr 𝔟 = x, 𝔟 ⊆ Λ, [𝔟] ∈ [𝔤]Pic(Λ)²}, where 𝒥(Λ)_0 = 𝒥(Λ) ∪ {0·Λ}. Let r : N → N be the multiplicative function defined by the following values, for k ≥ 1. For an odd prime p | D at which B splits, r(p^k) = 1 if k < ord_p D and r(p^k) = 2 if k ≥ ord_p D. If 2 | D, r(2^k) = 2^{μ_wild}, with μ_wild = ord_2[Z_2^× : Nr Λ_2^×] as in Corollary A.7. If p | D and B ramifies at p, r(p^k) = 2. For p ∤ D, r(p^k) = 1.
items.locator: §8.2, Definition 8.6, p. 203 (arXiv v3: Definition 85)
items.note: The multiplicative functions whose shifted convolution the main estimate bounds. They are the ideal-counting functions of a quadratic order; AN.5 plans mean values of multiplicative functions but not these. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: f_{[𝔤]} is not 'analogous' to g_{[𝔤]}. g_{[𝔤]} counts 𝔞 ∈ 𝒥(Λ)_0 = 𝒥(Λ) ∪ {0·Λ} in the CLASS [𝔤], with 𝔞 = 0 allowed. f_{[𝔤]} counts invertible integral 𝔟 in the GENUS [𝔤]Pic(Λ)². The same definition introduces the multiplicative weight r, which Theorem 8.7 uses; the item omits it. Print says μ_wild ∈ {0,1,2,3}, although Corollary A.7 gives {0,1,2} (source issue).

items.name: The cross-correlation as a shifted convolution sum
items.statement: Fix a joint homogeneous toral set [T^Δ(A)(g,sg)] with splitting field E/Q and quadratic order Λ ≤ O_E of discriminant D satisfying (♠): g_∞^{-1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞, g_{p_1}^{-1}T(Q_{p_1})g_{p_1} = A_{p_1} and g_{p_2}^{-1}T(Q_{p_2})g_{p_2} = A_{p_2}. Let B = ∏_v B_v ⊂ G(A) with B_v = Ω_v for all v ≠ p_1 and B_{p_1} = K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)} for some n ∈ N. Fix a simply connected homogeneous Hecke set [G^Δ(A)^+ξ] with ctr(ξ)_{p_1} ∈ A_{p_1}, and assume g^{-1}T(Q)sg ∩ B ctr(ξ) B = ∅. Let μ and ν be the algebraic probability measures on [T^Δ(A)(g,sg)] and [G^Δ(A)^+ξ]. Put κ = 2^8·𝔡_∞(ctr(ξ)_∞)·𝔡_f(ctr(ξ)_f) and ω = −sign(Nrd(ctr(ξ)_∞))·𝔡_f(ctr(ξ)_f). Then Cor[μ,ν](B) ≪ vol([T(A)g])^{-1}·vol([G^Δ(A)^+ξ])^{-1}·p_1^{−2n}·Σ_{0≤x≤κ|D|, x≡ωD mod υp_1^{2n}} g_{[𝔰]}(x)·f_{[p_1^n𝔰𝔢]^{-1}}((x−ωD)/(υp_1^{2n}))·r((x−ωD)/(υp_1^{2n})). Here υ is supported on primes inert in E/Q while p_1 splits, so gcd(υ, p_1^{2n}) = 1.
items.locator: §8.2, Theorem 8.7 and Remark 8.8, p. 203; proof in §8.8, pp. 218–220 (arXiv v3: Theorem 86 with Remark 87)
items.note: The bridge between the dynamics and analytic number theory, and the technical heart of the paper: the correlation of a toral packet with a Hecke correspondence is a shifted convolution of ideal-counting functions. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Hypotheses are missing and the bound is left unstated. Omitted: condition (♠) on g; the hypothesis ctr(ξ)_{p_1} ∈ A_{p_1}; the non-containment hypothesis g^{-1}T(Q)sg ∩ B ctr(ξ) B = ∅, without which the theorem is false; the values of κ and ω; and the exact bound, which has the factor vol([T(A)g])^{-1}vol([G^Δ(A)^+ξ])^{-1}p_1^{-2n} and the weight r.

items.name: The rational double quotient W_Q and the dagger subgroups
items.statement: Set W_Q = G^Δ(Q)\(G × G)(Q)/T^Δ(Q), with a natural map to W(Q). For a closed subgroup N < M(A) write N^† = N ∩ (G(A)^+ × T(A)), always normal in N.
items.locator: §8.3, Definitions 8.9 and 8.10, pp. 203–204 (arXiv v3: Definitions 88 and 89)
items.note: The index set of the geometric expansion and the subgroups through which the orbital integrals are taken.

items.name: Geometric expansion of the cross-correlation
items.statement: Let μ be the periodic measure on a joint homogeneous toral set [T^Δ(A)(g,sg)] and ν the periodic measure on a simply connected Hecke correspondence [G^Δ(A)^+ξ], with ξ = (ξ_1,ξ_2). Let M = G × T act on G × G by (l,t).(g_1,g_2) = (lg_1t^{-1}, lg_2t^{-1}), let M_γ be the stabiliser of γ, and put B′ = ξ_1Bg^{-1} × ξ_2Bg^{-1}s^{-1}. Then Cor[μ,ν](B) = ∫_{[G(A)^+]}∫_{[T(A)]} K_{B′}(l,t) dl dt = Σ_{[γ]∈W_Q} Σ_{κ∈π_G(M_γ(Q))\G(Q)/G(Q)^+} vol(M_γ)·RO_{γ,κ}(B). Here RO_{γ,κ}(B) := ∫_{M_γ(A)^†\M(A)^†} 1_{B′}((κl)^{-1}γt) d(l,t) and vol(M_γ) := m_{M_γ(A)^†}(M_γ(Q)^†\M_γ(A)^†), with the Haar measures on M_γ(A)^†\M(A)^† and M_γ(A)^† mutually normalised.
items.locator: §8.3, Proposition 8.11, p. 204; proof pp. 205–206 (arXiv v3: Proposition 90)
items.note: The unfolding that turns the correlation into a sum over rational orbits, in the manner of a relative trace formula. Nothing in the atlas plans relative orbital integrals for the pair (G^Δ, T^Δ) in G × G. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Incomplete. The expansion is a double sum, over [γ] ∈ W_Q and over κ ∈ π_G(M_γ(Q))\G(Q)/G(Q)^+, with weights vol(M_γ). The orbital integral is taken over M_γ(A)^†\M(A)^† with mutually normalised Haar measures.

items.name: Invariance of Haar measure under conjugation on the dagger subgroup
items.statement: For a ∈ M(A), conjugation Ad_a : M(A)^† → M(A)^† preserves any Haar measure on M(A)^†.
items.locator: §8.3, Lemma 8.12, p. 204 (arXiv v3: Lemma 91)
items.note: The unimodularity needed for the orbital integrals to be well defined.

items.name: Relative orbital integrals
items.statement: Fix γ ∈ (G×G)(Q) with M_γ(A) compact, so that M_γ(Q) is finite. With the Haar measure of M_γ(A)^† normalised to mass 1, RO_{γ,κ}(B) = ∫_{M(A)^†} 1_{B′}((κl)^{-1}γt) d(l,t), and Σ_{κ∈π_G(M_γ(Q))\G(Q)/G(Q)^+} vol(M_γ)·RO_{γ,κ}(B) = (#M_γ(Q))^{-1}·Σ_{κ∈G(Q)/G(Q)^+} RO_{γ,κ}(B). For κ ∈ G(Q), RO_{γ,κ}(B) = RO^∞_{γ,κ}(B)·RO^f_{γ,κ}(B), where RO^∞_{γ,κ}(B) := ∫_{M(R)^†} 1_{B′_∞}((κl)^{-1}γt) d(l,t) and RO^f_{γ,κ}(B) := ∫_{M(A_f)^†} 1_{B′_f}((κl)^{-1}γt) d(l,t).
items.locator: §8.3, Lemma 8.13, p. 206; §8.5, Definition 8.17, p. 208 (arXiv v3: Lemma 92 with Definition 96)
items.note: The local decomposition of the geometric expansion. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Imprecise. The formula RO = ∫_{M(A)^†} holds only after normalising the Haar measure of the compact group M_γ(A)^† to mass 1. The identity it yields is not stated in the item. Print's Definition 8.17 writes RO_{γ,κ}(B) = RO^∞_γ(B)·RO^f_γ(B), dropping κ on the right.

items.name: Reduction to compact stabilisers
items.statement: Assume g^{-1}T(Q)sg ∩ B^{-1}ctr(ξ)B = ∅. Then RO_{γ,ϰ}(B) = 0 for every γ with non-compact M_γ(A)^†, and consequently Cor[μ, ν](B) equals the sum over [γ] ∈ W_Q with ψ det^{-1}(γ) ≠ 0 of the corresponding orbital integrals, divided by #M_γ(Q).
items.locator: §8.4, Lemma 8.14 and Corollary 8.16, pp. 207–208 (arXiv v3: Lemma 93 with Corollary 95)
items.note: The step that discards the terms with non-compact stabiliser, which would otherwise dominate; the hypothesis is exactly that the Hecke correspondence does not already contain the packet.

items.name: Bound on the non-archimedean orbital integral
items.statement: For [γ] ∈ W_Q, Σ_ϰ RO^f_{γ,ϰ}(B) ≤ 2·m_{G(A_f)}(B_{G,f})·m_{T(A_f)}(B_{T,f})·N_{[γ]}, where N_{[γ]} counts the number of times the M(A_f)-orbit of γ meets B′_f modulo B_{M,f}. This uses that each coset of M(A_f)/B_{M,f} contains at most two cosets of G(Q)M(A_f)^†/B_{M,f}^†.
items.locator: §8.7.1, Lemma 8.21 and Proposition 8.23, pp. 210–211 (arXiv v3: Lemma 100 with Proposition 102)
items.note: The reduction of the non-archimedean orbital integral to a counting problem for the orbits of M on the affine variety G.

items.name: Contraction of the counting function N_{[γ]}
items.statement: Let M = G × T act on the affine variety G, with the G-coordinate acting trivially and the T-coordinate by conjugation. The contraction ctr : G×G → G, (g_1,g_2) ↦ g_1^{-1}g_2, is an M-equivariant morphism of affine varieties. The set B′_f = ξ_{1,f}B_fg_f^{-1} × ξ_{2,f}B_fg_f^{-1}s_f^{-1} ⊂ (G×G)(A_f) is B_{M,f}-invariant, and ctr induces a bijection B_{M,f}\B′_f → Ad B_{T,f}\ctr(B′_f). In particular, for every γ ∈ (G×G)(Q), N_{[γ]} = #(Ad B_{T,f}\(Ad T(A_f)ctr(γ) ∩ ctr(B′_f))).
items.locator: §8.7.1, Lemma 8.24, pp. 211–212 (arXiv v3: Lemma 103)
items.note: The reduction of the counting problem to the adjoint quotient, where the invariants of Section 5 apply. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The claim that 'B′_f is a union of Ad T(A_f)-orbits' is not in the paper and is false in general. The lemma says that B′_f is B_{M,f}-invariant, and that ctr induces a bijection B_{M,f}\B′_f → Ad B_{T,f}\ctr(B′_f). The item also omits the resulting formula for N_{[γ]}.

items.name: Bound on the archimedean orbital integral
items.statement: For γ ∈ (G × G)(Q) and ϰ ∈ G(Q) with B_∞ = Ω_∞: RO^∞_{γ,ϰ}(B) = 0 unless ctr(γ) ∈ g_∞Ω_∞ctr(ξ)_∞Ω_∞g_∞^{-1}, and otherwise it is bounded by the product of the volumes of T(R) and of an explicit compact set.
items.locator: §8.6, Lemma 8.18, p. 209 (arXiv v3: Lemma 97)
items.note: The archimedean estimate, which is where the compactness of the real torus K_∞ is used.

items.name: The invariant map inv
items.statement: Let K_{T,f} := T(A_f) ∩ g_fK_fg_f^{-1}. Define inv_f : Ad K_{T,f}\G(A_f) → Q^×_Δ\(𝒥(Λ)_0 × 𝒥(Λ)_0) as follows. For v ≠ ∞, write a representative of h_v in B^×(Q_v) in the coordinates of Proposition 5.19 as h_v = Q_v^×·(α_v, β_vυ_vτ_v ; ^σβ_v/τ_v, ^σα_v) with α_v, β_v ∈ E_v. Set inv_f([h_f]) := (idl~(α_v), idl~(β_v)) = (∩_{v≠∞} α_vΛ_v, ∩_{v≠∞} β_vΛ_v). The pair is well defined up to multiplying both entries by one element of Q^×, since Q has class number one. It is invariant under conjugation by K_{T,f}, which multiplies β_v by an element of cbd(Λ_v^×) ⊂ Λ_v^×. Put G(A)_accessible := Ad T(A)G(Q), an Ad T(A)-invariant subset of G(A). Define inv : Ad T(R)Ad K_{T,f}\G(A)_accessible → Q^×\(𝒥(Λ)_0 × 𝒥(Λ)_0) by applying inv_f to the finite part. On accessible elements the local maps π_W : Ad T(Q_v)\G(Q_v) → W(Q_v) take a common value in W(Q) at every place; this defines π_W : Ad T(A)\G(A)_accessible → W(Q).
items.locator: §8.7.2, Definitions 8.25 and 8.26, pp. 212–213 (arXiv v3: Definitions 104 and 105)
items.note: The arithmetic invariant that classifies the orbits appearing in the geometric expansion; it is the paper's replacement for the classical parametrisation of Hecke orbits by ideals. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The target of inv_f is wrong. inv_f takes values in Q^×_Δ\(𝒥(Λ)_0 × 𝒥(Λ)_0): pairs of invertible FRACTIONAL ideals, possibly zero, modulo simultaneous scaling by Q^×. The item has 'pairs of homothety classes of integral ideals'. The construction and the map π_W of Definition 8.26(3) are missing.

items.name: The fibres of the invariant map
items.statement: Let [T(A)g] be a homogeneous toral set and [h] ∈ Ad T(R)Ad K_{T,f}\G(A)_accessible with inv(h) ∈ Q^×\(𝒥(Λ)_0 × 𝒥(Λ)), i.e. h ∉ T(Q). Then ∏_{v≠∞} H^1(𝔊, Λ_v^×) acts faithfully on inv^{-1}(inv([h])), with at most 8 orbits. The fibres of inv × π_W are principal homogeneous spaces for this group, and π_W takes at most 8 values on inv^{-1}(inv([h])). Consequently #inv^{-1}(inv([h])) ≪ #Pic(Λ)[2], by Corollary A.12.
items.locator: §8.7.2, Proposition 8.27 and Corollary 8.28, pp. 213–215 (arXiv v3: Proposition 106 with Corollary 107)
items.note: The multiplicity bound for the invariant: each pair of ideals is hit boundedly often, by a 2-torsion factor, which is exactly the loss one can afford. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Omits the bound of at most 8 orbits. That bound, together with Corollary A.12, is what gives the corollary. The fibre is inv^{-1}(inv([h])); print writes inv^{-1}([h]) and '≪ Pic(Λ)[2]' for '≪ #Pic(Λ)[2]' (source issue).

items.name: The ideal classes of the invariants
items.statement: If h = tγt^{-1} with t ∈ T(A) and γ ∈ G(Q), and inv(h) = Q^×(𝔞, 𝔟), then [𝔞] = 1 in Pic(Λ) when 𝔞 ≠ 0, and [𝔟𝔢] ∈ Pic(Λ)² when 𝔟 ≠ 0.
items.locator: §8.7.2, Lemma 8.29, p. 215 (arXiv v3: Lemma 108)
items.note: The constraint on which ideal classes can occur, which is what makes the shifted convolution sum have the shape it does.

items.name: From intersections to invariants
items.statement: Fix (x_v)_v ∈ G(A); print has G(A_f), but x_∞ is used. Let B_v = Ω_v for v ≠ p_1 and B_{p_1} = K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)} ⊂ Ω_{p_1} for some n ∈ N. If h ∈ G(A)_accessible lies in ∏_v g_vB_v^{-1}x_vB_vg_v^{-1}s_v^{-1}, then inv(h) = Q^×Λ̂(𝔞·𝔰^{-1}, 𝔟·^σ𝔰^{-1}) for some 𝔞, 𝔟 ∈ 𝒥(Λ)_0 satisfying: (1) 𝔞, 𝔟 ⊆ Λ; (2) p_1^n | 𝔟; (3) Nr(𝔞) − υ·Nr(𝔟) = sign(Nrd(x_∞))·𝔡_f(x_f)·|D|; (4) Nr(𝔞) ≤ 2^8·𝔡_∞(x_∞)·𝔡_f(x_f)·|D|; (5) [𝔞] = [𝔰] in Pic(Λ) if 𝔞 ≠ 0; (6) [𝔟] ∈ [𝔰𝔢]^{-1}Pic(Λ)² if 𝔟 ≠ 0. Here Λ̂ is the inverse different of Λ (Definition 5.7), and υ, 𝔢 are as in Definition 8.4.
items.locator: §8.7.2, Proposition 8.30, pp. 215–217 (arXiv v3: Proposition 109)
items.note: The computation of the invariant of an element of the Hecke set, which produces the two ideals of the shifted convolution. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The six conditions on (𝔞,𝔟) are left out, and they are the whole content of the proposition. Print also writes '(x_v)_v ∈ G(A_f)' although (3) and (4) use x_∞, and at the end of the proof cites 'Claim (1)' for Claim (2) (source issue).

items.name: The fibre over an integral invariant at an odd ramified prime
items.statement: Let h ∈ G(A)_accessible with inv(h) = Q^×Λ̂(𝔞𝔰^{-1}, 𝔟·^σ𝔰^{-1}) as in Proposition 8.30, so that h ∈ ∏_v g_vB_v^{-1}x_vB_vg_v^{-1}s_v^{-1}. Let p | D be an odd prime at which B splits, and v the corresponding place. By Proposition 8.27, H^1(𝔊,Λ_v^×) acts faithfully on inv^{-1}(inv(h)); let −1 be its unique non-trivial element (Lemmas A.13, A.14). If ord_p Nr(𝔟) < ord_p D, then (−1).h_v ∉ g_vB_v^{-1}x_vB_vg_v^{-1}s_v^{-1}. With Proposition 8.27, the map from intersections to pairs (𝔞,𝔟) is therefore at most 8·r(Nr 𝔟)-to-one.
items.locator: §8.7.2, Proposition 8.32, pp. 217–218 (arXiv v3: Proposition 111)
items.note: The refinement of the multiplicity bound at the primes dividing the discriminant. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Both the name and the statement are wrong. The proposition concerns an odd prime p | D at which B SPLITS. Such a p need not be ramified in E: it may divide the conductor. It says that the non-trivial local class −1 ∈ H^1(𝔊,Λ_v^×) moves h out of the double coset when ord_p Nr(𝔟) < ord_p D. The item's 'can be computed explicitly' states nothing. This proposition is the source of the factor r(Nr 𝔟) in Theorem 8.7.

items.name: Measure of the Bowen balls at p_1
items.locator: §8.8, Lemma 8.33, p. 218 (arXiv v3: Lemma 112)
items.note: The volume computation that turns the Bowen-ball parameter n into the saving p_1^{2n} in the final estimate.

items.name: Solution counts of a binary polynomial
items.statement: (1) For Q ∈ Z[x,y] and a ∈ N, ρ_Q(a) := #{(x,y) ∈ Z²/aZ² : Q(x,y) ≡ 0 mod a} = #X_Q(Z/aZ), where X_Q := Spec Z[x,y]/(Q). (2) For a prime power p^k, a lift of x ∈ X_Q(Z/p^kZ) is a point of X_Q(Z/p^{k+1}Z) reducing to x mod p^k. Each point of X_Q(Z/p^k) is of one of three kinds: smooth (∇Q ≢ 0 mod p), with exactly p lifts by Hensel's lemma; singular with a lift, with exactly p² lifts; or singular without a lift. (3) ρ̃_Q(p^k) is the number of points of X_Q(Z/p^k) that are smooth or have no lift, extended multiplicatively to N; ρ̃_Q ≤ ρ_Q. (4) ρ^sing_Q(p^k) is the number of non-smooth points of X_Q(Z/p^k), i.e. those with 0 or p² lifts. (5) For k ∈ N and 0 ≤ l < k, ρ_Q(l;k) is the number of solutions mod k of Q(x,y) ≡ l. Thus ρ_Q(0;k) = ρ_Q(k) and ρ_Q(l;k) = ρ_{Q−l}(k).
items.locator: §9 (opening), Definition 9.1, p. 221; §9.7, Definition 9.24, p. 235 (arXiv v3: Definition 113 with Definition 136)
items.note: The local densities of a binary form.
