SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.0 plans sieve data and local densities in general; these counts for a plane curve, with the singular correction, are the specific input. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: ρ̃_Q is misdefined. ρ̃_Q(p^k) counts the points of X_Q(Z/p^k) that are smooth OR singular with no lift to Z/p^{k+1}. It excludes only the singular points that lift, each of which has exactly p² lifts. It is not a count of non-singular solutions, and it is extended multiplicatively. This is the paper's first new idea (p. 220), and Lemma 9.3 depends on it. Review note on status: SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.0 plans multiplicative local densities in general. ρ̃_Q and ρ^sing_Q are specific to this paper, so 'missing' is right.

items.name: The DeMillo–Lipton–Schwartz–Zippel bound
items.statement: For 0 ≠ Q ∈ Z[x,y] and any prime p not dividing Q, ρ_Q(p) ≤ deg(Q)·p.
items.locator: §9 (opening), Lemma 9.2, p. 221 (arXiv v3: Lemma 114)
items.note: The elementary bound on the number of zeros of a bivariate polynomial modulo a prime. Mathlib has the Schwartz–Zippel lemma for multivariate polynomials over an integral domain, but the statement here is for Z/p with the explicit constant deg(Q). Review note on status: Near miss in Mathlib. At the pinned commit 082e2d37, mathlib:MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree (Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/SchwartzZippel.lean, read) gives #{f ∈ S^n : eval f p = 0}/#S^n ≤ totalDegree p/#S for p ≠ 0 over a domain. With n = 2, R = ZMod p, S = univ, applied to Q mod p ≠ 0 (whose total degree is ≤ deg Q), this is the lemma. By §1 it stays 'missing', with this reduction as its proof step.

items.name: Singular and non-singular solution counts
items.statement: For 0 ≠ Q ∈ Z[x,y] and a prime power p^k, ρ̃_Q(p^k) = ρ_Q(p^k) − ρ^sing(p^{k+1})/p².
items.locator: §9 (opening), Lemma 9.3, pp. 221–222 (arXiv v3: Lemma 115)
items.note: The identity separating the singular contribution, which is what allows Hensel lifting to control the higher powers.

items.name: Convex domains of class L(C_l, θ_l) and the class M(A,B,ε)
items.statement: A convex domain E ⊂ R² is C² if its boundary is a C² curve. R_max(E) is the maximal radius of curvature of the boundary and A(E) is the area. For C_l, θ_l > 0, L(C_l,θ_l) is the set of C² convex planar domains E such that |#(a^{-1}(E − (x_0,y_0)) ∩ Z²) − a^{-2}A(E)| ≤ C_l·(R_max(E)/a)^{θ_l} for every a ∈ N with A(E) ≥ a² and every (x_0,y_0) ∈ Z². By van der Corput, for every ε > 0 there is C_l(ε) such that every C² convex domain lies in L(C_l, 2/3+ε). By Huxley, every ellipse lies in L(C_l, 131/208+ε). For A ≥ 1 and B, ε > 0, a multiplicative f : N → R is of class M(A,B,ε) if f ≥ 0 and f(n) ≤ min(A^{Ω(n)}, B·n^ε) for every n ≥ 1, where Ω(n) is the number of prime factors counted with multiplicity.
items.locator: §9 (opening), Definitions 9.4 and 9.6 and Remark 9.5, p. 222 (arXiv v3: Definitions 116 and 118 with Remark 117)
items.note: The geometric and arithmetic hypotheses of the sieve theorem; the lattice-point count for a convex domain is what GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans, and the class M(A,B,ε) is the divisor-type growth condition. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The class L(C_l,θ_l) is paraphrased too loosely. It is a lattice-point count in every residue class (x_0,y_0) mod a, for every a ∈ N with A(E) ≥ a², with error C_l(R_max/a)^{θ_l}. It is not a statement about homothetic copies. The item also omits Huxley's exponent 131/208 for ellipses. Review note on status: Ω is mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors at 082e2d37; the classes L and M are new.

items.name: A two-dimensional sieve for multiplicative functions along a binary polynomial
items.statement: Let E ⊂ R² be a planar domain of class L(C_l,θ_l) (C_l, θ_l > 0), with area A(E) and maximal radius of curvature R_max, and assume R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−3η} for some 1/2 > η > 0. Let Q ∈ Z[x,y], C > 0 and 1 ≥ r > 0 with ρ̃_Q(p^k) ≤ C·p^{k(2−r)} for all prime powers p^k. Let X ≥ 1 with max{|Q(x,y)| : (x,y) ∈ E∩Z²} ≤ X ≤ A(E)^δ for some δ > 0. Let f be a non-negative multiplicative function of class M(A,B,ε) with A ≥ 1, B > 0 and 0 < ε < min{r, ηr/(4δ)}. Then Σ_{(x,y)∈E∩Z²} f(Q(x,y)) ≪ A(E)·∏_{deg Q<p≤X, p∤Q}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²)·Σ_{a≤X} f(a)ρ̃_Q(a)/a², with the implied constant depending only on C_l, A, B, ε, deg Q, C, r, η, δ. (The paper leaves f(Q(x,y)) implicit where Q(x,y) ≤ 0; in the application f vanishes there.)
items.locator: §9 (opening), Theorem 9.7, pp. 222–223; proof in §9.6, pp. 231–235 (arXiv v3: Theorem 119)
items.note: The main analytic theorem of the paper: an upper bound of the expected order for the average of a multiplicative function along the values of a binary form over the lattice points of a convex domain, uniform in the domain and the form. It is a general sieve statement and is routed to the sieve roadmap rather than to the dynamical Part II. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague, and one hypothesis is wrong. The theorem needs max{|Q(x,y)| : (x,y) ∈ E∩Z²} ≤ X ≤ A(E)^δ for some δ > 0, and 0 < ε < min{r, ηr/(4δ)}; ε < r is not enough. The conclusion is the explicit inequality (34), with an implied constant depending only on C_l, A, B, ε, deg Q, C, r, η, δ. The proof has a gap in range R_2 (source issue).

items.name: A Mertens-type lower bound
items.statement: Let g : N → R be multiplicative with 0 ≤ g(p) ≤ d for all primes p. Then for any z > 1, Σ_{n ≤ z} μ(n)²g(n)/n ≫_d ∏_{d < p ≤ z}(1 − g(p)/p)^{-1}.
items.locator: §9.2, Lemma 9.8, pp. 223–224 (arXiv v3: Lemma 120)
items.note: The standard lower bound for the Selberg sieve weight.

items.name: The large sieve applied to a binary polynomial
items.statement: Let Q ∈ Z[x,y] and E ⊂ R² of class L(C_l,θ_l). If 1 ≤ z ≤ min{(A(E)/R_max^{θ_l})^{1/5}, A(E)^{1/2}}, then #{(x,y) ∈ E∩Z² : P^−(Q(x,y)) ≥ z} ≪_{deg Q, C_l} A(E)·∏_{deg Q<p≤z}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²), where P^−(n) is the smallest prime factor of n. The exponent 1/5 is not optimal, and any positive exponent would suffice (Remark 9.10).
items.locator: §9.2, Lemma 9.9 and Remark 9.10, pp. 224–225 (arXiv v3: Lemma 121 with Remark 122)
items.note: The large-sieve input. SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.2 plans the additive and multiplicative large-sieve inequalities and their duality; this is their application to the values of a binary form on a convex domain. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. The printed product runs over all deg(Q) < p ≤ z, with no p ∤ Q; when some p | Q has p ≤ z the bound is trivial. The implied constant depends on deg Q and C_l. The item's version, with p ∤ Q, is weaker but still true. Review note on status: SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2 plans the large-sieve inequality that this lemma applies, in Kowalski's setup. The lemma itself is missing.

items.name: Extending the level of distribution
items.statement: For Q ∈ Z[x,y], z ≥ 1 and s > 0, ∏_{deg Q < p ≤ z^{1/s}}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²) ≪_{deg Q} s^{deg Q}∏_{deg Q < p ≤ z, p ∤ Q}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²); consequently the previous bound holds for 1 ≤ z ≤ A(E)^{ς_0} whenever R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−η}.
items.locator: §9.3, Lemmas 9.11 and 9.12, pp. 225–226 (arXiv v3: Lemmas 123 and 124)
items.note: The step that removes the restrictive range of z from the large-sieve bound.

items.name: The sieve bound in a homogeneous arithmetic progression
items.statement: Let Q ∈ Z[x,y] and E ⊂ R² of class L(C_l,θ_l). Fix 1/2 > η > 0 and ς > 0, and assume R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−3η}. For a, z ∈ N with a ≤ A(E)^η and 1 ≤ z ≤ A(E)^ς: #{(x,y) ∈ E∩Z² : a | Q(x,y), gcd(a, Q(x,y)/a) = 1, P^−(Q(x,y)/a) ≥ z} ≪_{deg Q, C_l, η, ς} A(E)·(ρ̃_Q(a)/a²)·∏_{deg Q<p≤z, p∤a}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²). Without the gcd condition: #{(x,y) ∈ E∩Z² : a | Q(x,y), P^−(Q(x,y)/a) ≥ z} ≪_{deg Q, C_l, η, ς} A(E)·(ρ_Q(a)/a²)·∏_{deg Q<p≤z, p∤a}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²).
items.locator: §9.4, Lemma 9.13 and Corollary to Proof 9.14, pp. 226–227 (arXiv v3: Lemma 125 with Corollary 126)
items.note: The sieve bound with a divisibility condition, which is what the shifted convolution needs. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague. The main bound assumes gcd(a, Q(x,y)/a) = 1 and has the factor ρ̃_Q(a)/a². The variant without the gcd condition (Corollary to Proof 9.14) has ρ_Q(a)/a² in its place. The item omits the gcd condition from the main statement and states neither bound.

items.name: The auxiliary multiplicative function θ_Q
items.statement: For Q ∈ Z[x,y] let θ_Q be the multiplicative function with θ_Q(p^k) = 1 + 2ρ_Q(p)/p² if p ∤ Q and θ_Q(p^k) = 1 if p | Q, for k ≥ 1; here p | Q means that p divides every coefficient. Write θ_Q = 1 ∗ λ_Q. Then λ_Q(n) = μ(n)²·2^{ω(n)}·ρ_Q(n)/n² if gcd(n,Q) = 1, and λ_Q(n) = 0 otherwise. If f ∈ M(A,B,ε), then for every ε′ > 0, fθ_Q ∈ M(A′,B′,ε+ε′) with A′ ≪_{deg Q} A and B′ ≪_{ε′, deg Q} B (Remark 9.16). In the setting of Lemma 9.13 (Corollary 9.17): #{(x,y) ∈ E∩Z² : a | Q(x,y), gcd(a,Q(x,y)/a) = 1, P^−(Q(x,y)/a) ≥ z} ≪_{deg Q, C_l, η, ς} A(E)·(ρ̃_Q(a)/a²)·θ_Q(a)·∏_{deg Q<p≤z, p∤gcd(Q,a)}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²).
items.locator: §9.4, Definition 9.15, Remark 9.16 and Corollary 9.17, pp. 227–228 (arXiv v3: Definition 127 with Remark 128 and Corollary 129)
items.note: The weight that absorbs the divisor-type losses in the sieve. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Corollary 9.17, which the locator names, is not stated. The constants in Remark 9.16 are left unspecified.

items.name: Decoupling multiplicative functions
items.statement: Let g, ψ be non-negative multiplicative functions and h = 1 * ψ. Then for z ≥ 1, Σ_{a ≤ z} g(a)h(a) ≤ 𝔐_z(g, ψ)·Σ_{a ≤ z} g(a), with 𝔐_z(g,ψ) = ∏_{p ≤ z}[1 + Σ_{v=1}^{log z/log p} ψ(p^v)Σ_{j ≥ v} g(p^j)], and an upper bound for 𝔐_z in terms of h.
items.locator: §9.5, Lemma 9.18 and Remark 9.19, p. 228 (arXiv v3: Lemma 130 with Remark 131)
items.note: The decoupling inequality that separates the divisor weight from the counting function; it is a general statement about multiplicative functions and is the technical heart of the sieve section.

items.name: Averaged sieve bounds and exponential savings
items.statement: Let Q ∈ Z[x,y], C > 0 and 1 ≥ r > 0 with ρ̃_Q(p^k) ≤ C·p^{k(2−r)} for all prime powers. (a) (Lemma 9.20) If f ≥ 0 is multiplicative with f(n) < B·n^ε for some B > 0, r > ε > 0 and all n, then for every z ≥ 1, Σ_{a≤z} ρ̃_Q(a)f(a)θ_Q(a)/a² ≪_{deg Q, B, C, r, ε} Σ_{a≤z} ρ̃_Q(a)f(a)/a². (b) (Lemma 9.21) If f ∈ M(A,B,ε) with 0 < ε < r, then for all α, s > 0, z > 1 and κ with (r−ε)·log z/(2s) ≥ κ > 0, Σ_{z^α≤a≤z, P^+(a)≤z^{1/s}} ρ̃_Q(a)f(a)/a² ≪_{κ, A, B, ε, C, r, deg Q} exp(−sακ)·Σ_{a≤z} ρ̃_Q(a)f(a)/a². (c) (Lemma 9.23) For β > 0 and 1 ≥ α ≥ 0, Σ_{z^α≤a≤z, P^+(a)≤log z·log log z} ρ̃_Q(a)/a² ≪_{C, α, β} z^{−rα+β}. (Remark 9.22) If X_Q is smooth over Q, then ρ_Q(p^k) ≤ deg(Q)·p^k at primes of good reduction, so C and r depend only on the primes of bad reduction.
items.locator: §9.5, Lemmas 9.20, 9.21 and 9.23 and Remark 9.22, pp. 229–231 (arXiv v3: Lemmas 132, 133 and 135 with Remark 134)
items.note: The three averaging lemmas that give the saving in the final bound, in the smooth, rough and intermediate ranges. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The right-hand side of the first bound is elided ('≪ Σ_{a ≤ z} …'), and the second bound is described only as 'exponentially small in the parameters'.

items.name: The sieve with fixed congruence conditions
items.statement: (Proposition 9.25) Fix k_0 ∈ N. In the setting of Theorem 9.7, assume in addition (R_max/k_0)^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)/k_0² and X ≤ A(E)^δ·k_0^{1−2δ}. Then Σ_{(x,y)∈E∩Z², k_0|Q(x,y)} f(Q(x,y)/k_0) ≪ A(E)·∏_{deg Q<p≤X/k_0, p∤k_0, p∤Q}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²)·Σ_{a≤X/k_0} f(a)ρ̃_Q(k_0a)/(k_0a)², with the implied constant of Theorem 9.7. (Proposition 9.26) In the setting of Theorem 9.7, assume in addition R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−4η} and X ≤ A(E)^{δ/2}. Let k_0, k_1, k_2 ∈ N be such that every prime dividing k_1 divides k_2, gcd(k_0,k_2) = 1 and k := k_0k_1k_2 ≤ A(E)^{η/2}, and let l ∈ (Z/k_2Z)^×. Then Σ_{(x,y)∈E∩Z², Q(x,y)≡k_0k_1l mod k} f(Q(x,y)/k_0) ≪ A(E)·f(k_1)·(ρ_Q(k_1l; k_1k_2)/(k_1k_2)²)·∏_{deg Q<p≤X/(k_0k_1), p∤k_0k_2, p∤Q}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²)·Σ_{a≤X/(k_0k_1), gcd(a,k_2)=1} f(a)ρ̃_Q(k_0a)/(k_0a)², with the implied constant of Theorem 9.7.
items.locator: §9.7, Propositions 9.25 and 9.26, pp. 235–237 (arXiv v3: Propositions 137 and 138)
items.note: The forms of the sieve theorem actually used in the application, where the shifted convolution comes with congruence conditions imposed by the ideals 𝔰 and 𝔢. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Only described, not stated. The exact hypotheses and bounds follow.

items.name: Reduction of the main theorem to a bound on cross-correlation
items.statement: Notation: for n ≥ 0, B^{(−n,n)} := ∏_{v≠p_1} Ω_v × K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)} ⊂ G(A), and B := B^{(−0,0)}. For ξ ∈ (G×G)(A), ν_ξ is the algebraic probability measure on [G^Δ(A)^+ξ]. Let H_i = [T_i^Δ(A)(g_i,s_ig_i)] be a sequence of homogeneous toral sets satisfying (♠) for all i, let μ_i be the algebraic measure on H_i, and assume μ_i → μ weak-*. Suppose there are a continuous F : G(A) → R_{>0} and a fixed ρ > 0 such that Cor[μ_i, ν_ξ](B^{(−n,n)}) ≪ F(ctr(ξ))·p_1^{−2(1+ρ)n} for all n ∈ N, all ξ ∈ (G×G)(A) and all i ≫_{n,ξ} 1. Then μ is a (G×G)(A)^+-invariant probability measure.
items.locator: §10.1, Lemma 10.1, pp. 237–239 (arXiv v3: Lemma 139)
items.note: The logical structure of the proof: rigidity leaves two possibilities, and the cross-correlation bound eliminates the Hecke one. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Hypothesis and conclusion are both misstated. The hypothesis is a power saving: Cor[μ_i,ν_ξ](B^{(−n,n)}) ≪ F(ctr ξ)·p_1^{−2(1+ρ)n} for a continuous F : G(A) → R_{>0}, a fixed ρ > 0, all n, all ξ, and all i ≫_{n,ξ} 1. It is not 'o of the corresponding volume'. The conclusion is that μ is (G×G)(A)^+-invariant; the proof excludes Hecke components by an entropy argument using [ELMV09, Prop. 3.2]. The item's 'convex combination of Haar measures' is not the conclusion. B^{(−n,n)} and ν_ξ, defined in the opening of §10, are needed.

items.name: From a shifted convolution to a binary quadratic form
items.statement: Let κ, υ, n be as in Theorem 8.7 and ω = −sign(Nrd(ctr(ξ)_∞))·𝔡_f(ctr(ξ)_f). Fix a Z-basis A, B ∈ E^× of the fractional Λ-ideal 𝔰^{-1}, and let q(x,y) := Nr(Ax+By)/Nr(𝔰^{-1}); it is a primitive, positive-definite, integral binary quadratic form of discriminant D. Put Q(x,y) := q(x,y) − ωD. Then Σ_{0≤x≤κ|D|, x≡ωD mod υp_1^{2n}} g_{[𝔰]}(x)·f_{[p_1^n𝔰𝔢]^{-1}}((x−ωD)/(υp_1^{2n}))·r((x−ωD)/(υp_1^{2n})) = (#Λ^×)^{-1}·Σ_{(x,y)∈Z², q(x,y)≤κ|D|, υp_1^{2n}|Q(x,y)} (f_{[p_1^n𝔰𝔢]^{-1}}·r)(Q(x,y)/(υp_1^{2n})). The proof uses that an integral 𝔞 lies in [𝔰] iff 𝔞 = a𝔰 with a ∈ 𝔰^{-1}, and that a is unique up to Λ^×.
items.locator: §10.2, Lemma 10.2, p. 240 (arXiv v3: Lemma 140)
items.note: The identification of the shifted convolution with a sum along a binary quadratic form, which is what makes the two-dimensional sieve applicable. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 and GN.3 plan binary quadratic forms, their reduction and their class theory. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague: 'an explicit region'. The printed lemma also has a sign slip (source issue). §10.2 redefines ω = +sign(Nrd(ctr(ξ)_∞))𝔡_f(ctr(ξ)_f), the negative of Theorem 8.7's ω, and writes x ≡ ω|D|, while keeping x − ωD and Q = q − ωD. The corrected statement below uses Theorem 8.7's ω throughout.

items.name: The ellipse and its curvature
items.statement: Taking q to be the reduced norm form of 𝔰^{-1} and E = {(x,y) : q(x,y) ≤ κ|D|}, the set E is an ellipse centred at the origin with area A(E) = 2πκ√|D| and maximal radius of curvature R_max ≤ √(A(E))·(√|D|/𝔑)^{3/2}, where 𝔑 is the minimal norm of an integral ideal in the class of 𝔰.
items.locator: §10.2, Definition 10.3 and Lemma 10.4, pp. 240–242 (arXiv v3: Definition 141 with Lemma 142)
items.note: The geometric input: the eccentricity of the ellipse is controlled by 𝔑, so the hypothesis 𝔑 → ∞ of the mixing conjecture is exactly what makes the domain admissible for the sieve. This is the point at which the arithmetic hypothesis becomes a geometric one.

items.name: The ideal-counting multiplicative functions
items.statement: Let f : N → N be f(n) := #{𝔞 ∈ 𝒥(Λ) : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ, Nr 𝔞 = n}, the multiplicative count of integral invertible Λ-ideals of norm n. Let r_0 : N → Z be the multiplicative function with r_0(p^k) = 2 if p | D_large and k ≥ ord_p D, and r_0(p^k) = 1 otherwise. Here D = D_small·D_large is the splitting of §10.2; see the proposed new item on D_small.
items.locator: §10.2, Definition 10.5, p. 242 (arXiv v3: Definition 143)
items.note: The arithmetic functions of the final estimate; the hypothesis that there is no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero enters through the size of the class number and hence through the average of f. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: r_0 is wrong. r_0(p^k) = 2 exactly when p | D_large and k ≥ ord_p D, and r_0(p^k) = 1 otherwise. The item has 'k ≥ 1' and leaves the remaining values unspecified.

items.name: Two elementary local lemmas
items.statement: (Lemma 5.16) Let π be a uniformiser of Z_v. Then a, b ∈ Q_v satisfy |a − b|_v ≤ 1 iff either (1) a, b ∈ Z_v, or (2) |a|_v = |b|_v = |π|_v^{−n} for some n ∈ Z and a/b ≡ 1 mod π^nZ_v. (Lemma 5.10) Regard E_v as a 2-dimensional Q_v-vector space. If B(Q_v) is split, there is an isomorphism of Q_v-algebras B(Q_v) ≃ End_{Q_v}(E_v) under which E(Q_v) ≃ E_v acts by multiplication. Moreover, there is a Q_v-linear isomorphism B(Q_v) ≃ E_v ⊕ E_v such that (α,β).a = α·a + β·^σa for all a ∈ E_v.
items.locator: §5.3, Lemma 5.16, p. 188, and Lemma 5.10, p. 185 (arXiv v3: Lemma 49 with Lemma 43)
items.note: An elementary p-adic lemma used repeatedly in Section 4. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Lemma 5.10 (arXiv Lemma 43), which the locator names, is not stated. The closing sentence about Λ̂_v is not the content of either lemma.

items.name: Local invariance groups for the orbital integrals
items.statement: Let B_f < G(A_f) be a compact-open subgroup, and fix a homogeneous Hecke set [G^Δ(A)^+(ξ_1,ξ_2)] and a homogeneous toral set [T(A)g]. Put B_{G,f} := ξ_{1,f}B_fξ_{1,f}^{-1} ∩ ξ_{2,f}B_fξ_{2,f}^{-1} < G(A_f), B^+_{G,f} := B_{G,f} ∩ G(A_f)^+, B_{T,f} := g_fB_fg_f^{-1} ∩ T(A_f), B_{M,f} := B_{G,f} × B_{T,f} < M(A_f) and B^†_{M,f} := B^+_{G,f} × B_{T,f} < M(A_f)^†. Each is a compact-open subgroup of its group. For γ ∈ (G×G)(Q) and κ ∈ G(Q), put f_{γ,κ}(l,t) := 1_{B′_f}((κl)^{-1}γt) and f_γ(l,t) := 1_{B′_f}(l^{-1}γt). Then f_{γ,κ} is B^†_{M,f}-invariant on M(A_f)^†, and f_γ is B_{M,f}-invariant on M(A_f).
items.locator: §8.7, Definitions 8.19 and 8.20, p. 210 (arXiv v3: Definitions 98 and 99)
items.note: The bookkeeping of invariance groups under which the non-archimedean orbital integrals are computed. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor. f_{γ,κ} is B^†_{M,f}-invariant on M(A_f)^†, but f_γ is B_{M,f}-invariant on M(A_f), which is not a dagger group. The groups B_{T,f}, B_{M,f} and B^†_{M,f} are only named in the item.

items.name: Reduction of the final shifted convolution to a congruence average
items.statement: With D_small, D_large, k = υp_1^{2n}D_small² and the measure w_k on Z/kZ as in §10.2, and E, Q as in Lemma 10.2 and Definition 10.3: (#Λ^×)^{-1}·Σ_{(x,y)∈E∩Z², υp_1^{2n}|Q(x,y)} (f_{[p_1^n𝔰𝔢]^{-1}}·r)(Q(x,y)/(υp_1^{2n})) ≪_G ∫ Σ_{(x,y)∈E∩Z², Q(x,y)≡m mod k} (f·r_0)(Q(x,y)/(υp_1^{2n})) dw_k(m). (Remark 10.7) Unlike that of r, the mean value of r_0 is bounded in terms of η alone, independently of D. The part of r not covered by r_0 is cancelled by the genus restriction when p | D_small and p ∥ Q(x,y).
items.locator: §10.2, Lemma 10.6 and Remark 10.7, p. 244 (arXiv v3: Lemma 144 with Remark 145)
items.note: The step that puts the sum in the shape the sieve theorem accepts. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The weights w_k are not defined in any item (proposed new item below). The inequality is ≪_G, with the factor (#Λ^×)^{-1} on the left.

items.name: Admissible lattice-point exponents and the decomposition of D_small
items.statement: An exponent θ_l > 0 is admissible if there is C_l > 0 such that every ellipse defined by a definite integral binary quadratic form belongs to the class L(C_l, θ_l); van der Corput's bound makes every θ_l > 2/3 admissible and Huxley's bound every θ_l > 131/208. For m ∈ Z/k and i ∈ {0,1,2} put D_i(m) = ∏_{p | D_small, ord_p m = i} p, so that D_small = D_0(m)D_1(m)D_2(m).
items.locator: §10.3, Definitions 10.8 and 10.9, p. 245 (arXiv v3: Definitions 146 and 147)
items.note: The lattice-point counting exponent for ellipses, which is exactly the classical divisor-problem exponent; GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans lattice-point estimates for convex bodies, and van der Corput's and Huxley's bounds are the inputs quoted here.

items.name: Applying the sieve to the shifted convolution
items.statement: Let m ∈ Z/kZ with w_k(m) > 0, let θ_l > 0 be admissible and 0 < η < 1/2, and assume R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−4η} (see the issue: 1−16η is what the proof supports) and υp_1^{2n} ≤ |D|^{η/2}. Then Σ_{(x,y)∈E∩Z², Q(x,y)≡m mod k} (f·r_0)(Q(x,y)/(υp_1^{2n})) ≪_{𝔣,η} A(E)·(ρ_Q(m; (D_0(m)D_1(m))²)/(D_0(m)D_1(m))⁴)·∏_{2<p≤2κ|D|^{1−η}, p∤υp_1D_small}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²)·Σ_{a≤2κ|D|, gcd(a,D_0(m)D_1(m))=1} f(a)·r_0(a)·ρ̃_Q(υp_1^{2n}D_2(m)²a)/(υp_1^{2n}D_2(m)²a)².
items.locator: §10.3, Proposition 10.10, pp. 245–246 (arXiv v3: Proposition 148)
items.note: The application of the two-dimensional sieve to the sum produced by the geometric expansion. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague: 'an explicit product'. The proof's check of the hypotheses of Proposition 9.26 is also faulty (source issue on p. 246). Since η is at the author's disposal, the argument goes through with δ = 4 and with 4η in place of η in Proposition 9.26, i.e. under R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−16η} and 0 < η < 1/8.

items.name: The local density bound for the shifted form
items.statement: Let m ∈ Z/kZ with w_k(m) > 0, and a ∈ N with gcd(a, D_0(m)D_1(m)) = 1. Then ρ̃_Q(υp_1^{2n}D_2(m)²a)/(υp_1^{2n}D_2(m)²a)² ≪_{𝔣,G} (|ω|²/(p_1^{2n}D_2(m)²a))·∏_{p|a}(1 + 1/p)·∏_{p|D_2(m)} 2(1 − 1/p)·r_1(a). Here r_1 is the multiplicative function with r_1(p^k) = 2 for p | D_large and k > ord_p D_large, and r_1(p^k) = 1 otherwise; r_1 ≤ r_0.
items.locator: §10.3, Lemma 10.11 and Remark 10.12, p. 246 (arXiv v3: Lemma 149 with Remark 150)
items.note: The estimate of the local densities of the shifted form, which produces the saving p_1^{-2n}. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: r_1 is not defined in the item, and the implied constant (≪_{𝔣,G}) is missing.

items.name: The logarithmic sums with the local densities
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 10.10: Σ_{(x,y)∈E∩Z², Q(x,y)≡m mod k} (f·r_0)(Q(x,y)/(υp_1^{2n})) ≪_{𝔣,η,G} A(E)·p_1^{−2n}·(ρ_Q(m; (D_0(m)D_1(m))²)/(D_0(m)D_1(m))⁴)·(2^{ω(D_2(m))}/D_2(m)²)·|ω|²·(log log(2|ω|))^8·∏_{2<p≤2κ|D|^{1−η}, p∤D_0(m)D_1(m)}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²)·Σ_{a≤2κ|D|, gcd(a,D_0(m)D_1(m))=1} f(a)/a.
items.locator: §10.3, Proposition 10.13, pp. 247–249 (arXiv v3: Proposition 151)
items.note: The intermediate bound, before the analytic input on L(1, χ_E). Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The factors 2^{ω(D_2(m))}/D_2(m)² and |ω|²(log log(2|ω|))^8 are missing, and the implied constant (≪_{𝔣,η,G}) is not stated.

items.name: The analytic number theory input
items.statement: Let m ∈ Z/kZ with w_k(m) > 0 and 1/2 > η > 0. If C > 0 satisfies L′(1,χ_E)/L(1,χ_E) ≤ C·log|D_E|, then ∏_{2<p≤2κ|D|^{1−η}, p∤D_0(m)D_1(m)}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²)·Σ_{a≤2κ|D|, gcd(a,D_0(m)D_1(m))=1} f(a)/a ≪_{C,η} L(1,χ_E)·∏_{p|𝔣}(1 − (D_E/p)/p) + |D|^{−1/3+o(1)}. Print has |D|^{−2/3+o(1)}. The implied constant also depends on 𝔣, through |L̃_g(1/2+it)| ≪_𝔣 |L(1/2+it,χ_E)|.
items.locator: §10.3, Proposition 10.14, pp. 250–251 (arXiv v3: Proposition 152)
items.note: This is the only place where the no-Siegel-zero hypothesis is used: it converts a sum of the ideal-counting function into the class number through L(1, χ_E), with the constant uniform in D. AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1 plans Dirichlet L-functions with their non-vanishing at 1 and AN.3 density estimates and explicit formulas; the exceptional-zero dichotomy in this quantitative form is what is assumed away. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The additive error term is dropped, and the local factor is elided as '∏_{p|𝔣}(…)'. The hypothesis L′/L(1,χ_E) ≤ C log|D_E| is IMPLIED by the absence of an exceptional zero, with C uniform in E (Hecke, via Landau, §10.4); the item's 'that is' treats the two as the same. Print's error term |D|^{−2/3+o(1)} does not follow from the proof, which gives |D|^{−1/3+o(1)} (source issue). Review note on status: The inputs are Hecke's bound (no exceptional zero ⇒ L′/L(1,χ) ≪ log|D|) and the Conrey–Iwaniec subconvexity bound |L(1/2+it,χ_E)| ≪ |D|^{1/6+o(1)}|1/2+it|^A. AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2 only labels exceptional zeros, and nothing in the atlas plans Conrey–Iwaniec. Neither is in the extraction's prerequisites.

items.name: The final bound on the shifted convolution
items.statement: Let θ_l > 0 be admissible and 0 < η < 1/2, and assume R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−4η} (1−16η; see item 96) and υp_1^{2n} ≤ |D|^{η/2}. Let C > 0 satisfy L′(1,χ_E)/L(1,χ_E) ≤ C·log|D_E|. With κ and ω as in Theorem 8.7: Σ_{0≤x≤κ|D|, x≡ωD mod υp_1^{2n}} g_{[𝔰]}(x)·f_{[p_1^n𝔰𝔢]^{-1}}((x−ωD)/(υp_1^{2n}))·r((x−ωD)/(υp_1^{2n})) ≪_{G,𝔣,η,C} κ·|ω|²·(log log(2|ω|))^8·√|D|·(L(1,χ_E) + |D|^{−1/3+o(1)})/p_1^{2n}.
items.locator: §10.3, Proposition 10.15, pp. 252–253 (arXiv v3: Proposition 153)
items.note: The estimate that completes the proof: the correlation of a packet with any Hecke correspondence is smaller than the trivial bound by a factor p_1^{2n}, which tends to zero as the Bowen balls shrink. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The sum is misquoted: '(x − ω)' should be (x − ωD), and the factor r((x−ωD)/(υp_1^{2n})) is dropped. The bound itself is not given. As printed, the proposition also has x ≡ w|D| (w for ω, and the ω-sign slip of §10.2) and the factor κ|ω|log(2|ω|), while its proof yields κ|ω|² and §10.4 uses κ|ω|². It also has the error term |D|^{−2/3+o(1)}, where the proof of Proposition 10.14 gives |D|^{−1/3+o(1)} (source issues).

items.name: The adelic form of Pic(Λ)/Pic(Λ)²
items.statement: The adelic norm Nr : A_E^× → A^× and the real adelic character χ_E attached to E/Q by global class field theory descend to a short exact sequence 1 → Pic(Λ)/Pic(Λ)² →^{Nr} Q^×\A^×/R_{>0}∏_vNr(Λ_v^×) →^{χ_E} {±1} → 1.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Proposition A.1, p. 257 (arXiv v3: Proposition 154)
items.note: Gauss's principal genus theorem in adelic form for an arbitrary quadratic order. The Tau Ceti roadmap on global number fields, layer 11, constructs orders and their Picard groups, and HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.0 the ring class fields and Artin maps; genus theory for a non-maximal order in this form is not planned. Review note on status: Pic of orders: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields Layer 11; the idele-class quotient: HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.0; the cyclic Hasse norm theorem used in the proof: tauceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 13. The statement itself is not planned, so 'missing' stands.

items.name: The genus index as a product of local norm indices
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Corollary A.2, p. 257 (arXiv v3: Corollary 155)
items.note: The local computation of the genus index. Review note on status: For maximal orders (𝔣 = 1), tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic Layer 3 plans Cl(K)/Cl(K)² ≅ Gal(K_gen/K) and the 2-rank t − 1 for imaginary K. That plausibly covers this index formula in that case; the non-maximal statement is missing.

items.name: Units of a non-maximal local order
items.statement: If Λ_v < O_{E_v} is non-maximal with conductor 𝔣_vO_{E_v} then 1 + 𝔣_vO_{E_v} ⊆ Λ_v^×, and under reduction modulo 𝔣_v one has Λ_v^× = red^{-1}((red Z)^×) = Z_v^× + 𝔣_vO_{E_v}.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Lemmas A.3 and A.4, p. 258 (arXiv v3: Lemmas 156 and 157)
items.note: The explicit description of the local unit group of a non-maximal order.

items.name: Norms of local units
items.statement: Fix v ≠ ∞ with residue characteristic p. (Lemma A.5) Nr O_{E_v}^× = Z_v^× if E_v/Q_v is unramified, and (Z_v^×)² if E_v/Q_v is ramified and p > 2. If 2 ramifies in E, Nr O_{E_2}^× is one of the three index-2 subgroups of Z_2^×, all of which contain (Z_2^×)² = 1 + 8Z_2. (Lemma A.6) Let Λ_v ⊊ O_{E_v} be non-maximal, with conductor 𝔣_vO_{E_v}. If p > 2, Nr Λ_v^× = (Z_v^×)². If p = 2: Nr Λ_2^× = Nr O_{E_2}^× if 2 ∥ 𝔣_2; Nr Λ_2^× = 1 + 4Z_2 if 4 ∥ 𝔣_2 and either E_2/Q_2 is unramified or Nr O_{E_2}^× = 1 + 4Z_2; and Nr Λ_2^× = 1 + 8Z_2 = (Z_2^×)² otherwise.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Lemmas A.5 and A.6, pp. 258–260 (Corollary A.7 and 'Corollary A.8', p. 260) (arXiv v3: Lemmas 158 and 159 with Corollaries 160 and 161)
items.note: The local norm computations that make the genus index explicit, including the dyadic cases. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: The p = 2 case of Lemma A.6 is given only as 'an explicit case distinction'. Corollary A.7 (arXiv Corollary 160), named in the locator, is not stated; it is proposed below as a separate item. 'Corollary 161' (printed Corollary A.8) is not a statement: it is the proof of Corollary A.7, typeset as a corollary (source issue). Review note on status: For 𝔣 = 1, see tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic Layer 3 (item 102). The non-maximal case is missing.

items.name: Kronecker characters
items.statement: For an odd prime p put p* = (−1)^{(p−1)/2}p ≡ 1 mod 4 and χ_p(n) = (p*/n), the unique non-trivial primitive real Dirichlet character of modulus p; and χ_4(n) = (−4/n), χ_8(n) = (8/n), the primitive real characters of modulus 4 and 8.
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Definition A.9, p. 260 (arXiv v3: Definition 162)
items.note: The characters cutting out the genera. Mathlib has the Jacobi and Kronecker symbols and quadratic reciprocity, but the packaging as the primitive real characters attached to a discriminant is what is used here. Review note on status: Mostly in the library. Mathlib at 082e2d37 has ZMod.χ₄, ZMod.χ₈ (= (8/·) on odd n) and ZMod.χ₈' (= χ₄χ₈) in Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/ZModChar.lean. It also has legendreSym and quadraticChar (ZMod p); χ_p(n) = (p*/n) = (n/p) by jacobiSym.quadratic_reciprocity. The prime discriminants p* appear in tauceti Multiquadratic Layer 1. Missing: only the (p*/·) packaging, the multiplicative extension to rationals prime to the modulus, and the adelic lifts.

items.name: The principal genus theorem
items.statement: Let 𝔞 ∈ 𝒥(Λ). Then [𝔞] ∈ Pic(Λ)² iff χ(Nr(𝔞)/gcd(Nr(𝔞), modulus(χ)^∞)) = 1 for each of the following real Dirichlet characters χ: (1) χ_p for every odd prime p | D; (2) one of χ_4, χ_8, χ_4χ_8, determined by the subgroup Nr Λ_2^× < Z_2^×, if [Z_2^× : Nr Λ_2^×] = 2; (3) χ_4 and χ_8 if Nr Λ_2^× = 1 + 8Z_2. There is no 2-adic condition when Nr Λ_2^× = Z_2^×.
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Proposition A.10, pp. 260–261 (Proposition A.11 and Corollary A.12, pp. 261–263) (arXiv v3: Propositions 163, 164 with Corollary 165)
items.note: Gauss's genus theory in the form the paper needs: membership in the principal genus is decided by finitely many Kronecker characters evaluated at the norm. This is what makes the ideal classes of the invariants of Section 7 detectable by congruence conditions. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Only Proposition A.10 is stated, and its 2-adic clause is wrong. Which 2-adic characters are needed depends on [Z_2^× : Nr Λ_2^×], not on whether 2 | D. There are none when the index is 1, which can happen with 2 | D (E unramified at 2 and 2 ∥ 𝔣). There is one of χ_4, χ_8, χ_4χ_8 when the index is 2, and both χ_4 and χ_8 when Nr Λ_2^× = 1 + 8Z_2. Proposition A.11 and Corollary A.12 (arXiv 164, 165), named in the locator, are not stated; they are proposed below as a separate item. Review note on status: For 𝔣 = 1, see tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic Layer 3 (genus field, Cl/Cl²). The order case is missing.

items.name: Galois cohomology of local unit groups and 2-torsion in Pic(Λ)
items.statement: Let v ≠ ∞. H^1(Q_v, O_{E_v}^×) = 1 if E_v/Q_v is unramified, and ≅ Z/2Z if it is ramified. If E_v/Q_v is tamely ramified (odd residue characteristic), the non-trivial class is the cocycle of −1 ∈ O_{E_v}^{(1)}. If Λ_v < O_{E_v} is non-maximal with residue characteristic p, then #H^1(𝔊, Λ_v^×) = 2 for p > 2 and 2^{μ_wild} for p = 2. For p > 2 its non-trivial class is represented by −1 ∈ Λ_v^{(1)}.
items.locator: Appendix A.3, Lemmas A.13 and A.14, pp. 263–264 (arXiv v3: Lemmas 166 and 167)
items.note: The cohomological computation behind the multiplicity bound for the invariant map, and the local description of the 2-torsion of the Picard group of the order. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Minor omission. In the tamely ramified maximal case, the non-trivial class of H^1(Q_v, O_{E_v}^×) is represented by −1 ∈ O_{E_v}^{(1)}. Proposition 8.32 uses this at odd p | D where Λ_v may be maximal.

items.name: Local diagonalisation of a binary quadratic form
items.statement: Let q be a primitive integral binary quadratic form of discriminant D < 0, and Q := q − ωD for some ω ∈ Z. For every prime p, q is Z_p-equivalent to a form q′ with Z_p-coefficients as follows. If p > 2, or p = 2 and D ≡ 0 mod 4, then q′ = ux² + Ay² with u ∈ Z_p^×; writing p^l ∥ A, A = u_A·p^l with u_A ∈ Z_p^×. If p = 2 and D ≡ 1 mod 4, then q′ = xy when D ≡ 1 mod 8 ((D/2) = +1), and q′ = x² + xy + y² when D ≡ −3 mod 8 ((D/2) = −1). (Remark B.2) Suppose q corresponds to the class [𝔰] ∈ Pic(Λ) and p > 2. Then (u/p) = χ_p(Nr[𝔰]), which depends only on [𝔰] mod Pic(Λ)². Write χ_p(q) := χ_p(Nr[𝔰]) = (u/p) for odd p | D. Since D = −4uA up to Z_p^{×2}, for p > 2 with p^l ∥ D, (u_A/p) = ((−D/p^l)/p)·χ_p(q).
items.locator: Appendix B.2, Lemma B.1 and Remark B.2, p. 265 (arXiv v3: Lemma 168 with Remark 169)
items.note: The local normal forms of a binary quadratic form. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 plans the quadratic local-global theory and GN.3 reduction; the Z_p-normal forms with the dyadic case are the specific input to the local density computation. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague. The item does not give the p = 2 normal forms, and 'invariants read off' stands in for the definition of χ_p(q) and for the relation it satisfies. The Appendix B setting (q primitive of discriminant D < 0, Q = q − ωD) is not recorded.

items.name: Local densities at regular primes
items.statement: If p ∤ ωD then ρ̃_Q(p^k) = ρ_Q(p^k) = ρ_Q(p)p^{k−1} and ρ_Q(p) = p − (D/p).
items.locator: Appendix B.3, Proposition B.3, pp. 265–266 (arXiv v3: Proposition 170)
items.note: The local density of the shifted form at the primes of good reduction, a Legendre-symbol count.

items.name: Local densities at singular primes
items.statement: Setting: q primitive of discriminant D < 0, Q = q − ωD, ω ∈ Z. (Lemma B.4, corrected) Let q_0 = u_1x² + u_2y² with u_1, u_2 ∈ Z_p^× (p odd), or p = 2 and q_0 ∈ {xy, x²+xy+y²}. Let u_3 ∈ Z_p^×, m ≥ 0, Q_m := q_0 − u_3p^m and d := (disc(q_0)/p). If m = 0, ρ_{Q_0}(p^n) = (p − d)·p^{n−1}. If 1 ≤ m and n ≤ m, ρ_{Q_m}(p^n) = ⌈n/2⌉·(p−1)(1+d)·p^{n−1} + p^n when n is even, and ⌈n/2⌉·(p−1)(1+d)·p^{n−1} + p^{n−1} when n is odd. If n > m: ρ_{Q_m}(p^n) = (m/2)·(p−1)(1+d)·p^{n−1} + (p−d)·p^{n−1} when m is even, and ((m+1)/2)·(p−1)(1+d)·p^{n−1} when m is odd. For p = 2 and q_0 diagonal, ρ_{Q_m}(2^n) ≤ min(⌈n/2⌉, 1+⌊m/2⌋)·2^{n+3} + 2^n (as printed; not rechecked). (Proposition B.5) Fix p | ωD, l := ord_p D and m := ord_p(4ω). For p > 2 put ρ^0_Q(p) := p − ((D/p^l)/p) if l is even; 2p if l is odd and (−ω/p) = χ_p(q); and 0 if l is odd and (−ω/p) = −χ_p(q). If p > 2 and n ≤ l, ρ_Q(p^n) = p^{n+⌊n/2⌋}; at p = 2 this is only an upper bound. If p > 2, n > l and p ∤ ω, ρ_Q(p^n) = p^{n+⌊l/2⌋}·ρ^0_Q(p)/p. If p > 2, n > l, p | ω and l is even, ρ_Q(p^n) = p^{l+l/2}·ρ_{Q_m}(p^{n−l}), from the corrected Lemma B.4 with d = ((D/p^l)/p). The printed closed forms for p | ω are wrong, and for l odd no correct closed form is available from the paper. If p = 2 and n > l, ρ_Q(2^n) ≤ 2^{n+⌈l/2⌉}·[min(⌈(n−l)/2⌉, 1+⌊m/2⌋)·2³ + 1]. (Corollary B.6) ρ_Q(p^n) ≤ 16·p^{n(2−1/2)} for every prime power. (Corollary B.7, corrected) Let p be an odd prime dividing D, and l = ord_p D. For n < l, ρ̃_Q(p^n) = p^{n+⌊n/2⌋}·(1 − 1/p) if n is even, and 0 if n is odd. If moreover p ∤ 4ω, then ρ̃_Q(p^l) = p^{l+⌊l/2⌋}·(1 − ρ^0_Q(p)/p²), and ρ̃_Q(p^n) = p^{n+⌊l/2⌋}·(ρ^0_Q(p)/p)·(1 − 1/p) for n > l.
items.locator: Appendix B.4, Lemma B.4, p. 266; Proposition B.5, p. 268; Corollaries B.6 and B.7, p. 269 (arXiv v3: Lemma 171 with Propositions 172 and Corollaries 173, 174)
items.note: The local densities at the bad primes. The uniform bound ρ_Q(p^n) ≤ 16p^{n(2−1/2)} is exactly the hypothesis ρ̃_Q(p^k) ≤ Cp^{k(2−r)} of the sieve theorem, with r = 1/2, so this is what makes the sieve applicable to the shifted norm form. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague. Several of the printed formulas it summarises are wrong; they were checked by direct counts of solutions mod p^n (source issues). Lemma B.4 is wrong for m ≥ 1. The first clause of Proposition B.5 fails at p = 2. The symbol (ω/p) in ρ^0_Q should be (−ω/p). The printed formula for p | ω with l odd is false. The first clause of Corollary B.7 is false at n = l and at p = 2. The corrected statement below gives what holds.

items.name: A genus-theoretic sum modulo p²
items.statement: Let p ∥ D, k ∈ {0,1}, p ∤ 4ω and ε ∈ {±1}. Then Σ_{a∈(Z/p^{2−k}Z)^×, (a/p)=ε} ρ_Q(p^k·a; p²) equals p⁴(1 − 1/p) if k = 0 and χ_p(q) = ε; 0 if k = 0 and χ_p(q) = −ε; and (p³/2)(1 − f/p) if k = 1. Here f := 1 + ε·((−D/p)/p)·χ_p(q) + ((−ω)/p)·χ_p(q) ∈ {−1, 1, 3}.
items.locator: Appendix B.4, Proposition B.8, pp. 270–271 (arXiv v3: Proposition 175)
items.note: The evaluation that ties the local densities to the genus character χ_p(q), so that the congruence conditions imposed by the ideal classes of the invariants can be summed. It is where the principal genus theory of the previous appendix meets the sieve. Review (REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague. The printed formula also has a sign error: with Q = q − ωD, the last term of f must be ((−ω)/p)χ_p(q), not (ω/p)χ_p(q). The two differ when p ≡ 3 mod 4. This was verified by direct count over 5,040 cases (source issue).

items.name: Special places and the standing normalisation (♠)
items.statement: Fix once and for all two finite primes p_1, p_2 at which G splits, maximal split tori A_{p_1} < G(Q_{p_1}) and A_{p_2} < G(Q_{p_2}) such that A_{p_1} ∩ K_{p_1} is maximal compact in A_{p_1} (equivalently, the apartment of A_{p_1} in the Bruhat–Tits tree contains the vertex fixed by K_{p_1}), and the maximal compact torus K_∞ < G(R) of §2.2.1. A homogeneous toral set [T(A)g], with T split at p_1 and p_2 and anisotropic at ∞, satisfies (♠) if g_∞^{-1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞, g_{p_1}^{-1}T(Q_{p_1})g_{p_1} = A_{p_1} and g_{p_2}^{-1}T(Q_{p_2})g_{p_2} = A_{p_2}. A joint set [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] satisfies (♠) if [T(A)g] does. Under (♠) the splitting field E of T is imaginary quadratic and split at p_1 and p_2, and the local discriminants D_∞, D_{p_1}, D_{p_2} are the same for all such sets.
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), §2.4.1 'Special places', display (♠), p. 163; §2.4.3, p. 164; Remark 2.5, p. 166 (arXiv v3: §2.4.1, eq. (♠), Remark 9)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): The standing normalisation used by every later statement (items 20, 26, 27, 42, 43, 52, 54 and Section 8). No item defines it: items 20 and 27 refer to 'the normalisation at p_1, p_2', and item 26 misdescribes A_{p_i}. Proposition 3.4 and Corollary 3.5 reduce the main theorem to sets satisfying (♠).

items.name: Maximal rational tori of B^× and of G
items.statement: Every maximal torus T < G defined over Q is the image of a unique maximal Q-torus T̃ < B^×. Every maximal Q-torus of B^× is T̃ = E^× ≅ Res_{E/Q}G_m, where E < B is the maximal commutative subalgebra with E(Q) = ι(E) for a ring embedding ι : E ↪ B(Q) of a quadratic étale Q-algebra E. E does not determine E, since there are inequivalent embeddings, but ι determines E up to automorphism. T = Z\T̃ ≅ G_m\Res_{E/Q}G_m is anisotropic over Q if and only if E is a field. For any lift of g to B^×(A), [T(A)g] = [T̃(A)g] in Z(A)B^×(Q)\B^×(A).
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), §2.4.3 'Homogeneous toral sets in B^×', p. 164 (arXiv v3 §2.4.3)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): Items 9, 10 and 16 use T̃ = E^× and 'the splitting field E' without the classification of maximal Q-tori, or the equivalence 'T anisotropic over Q ⟺ E a field'. Standard (maximal commutative subalgebras of a quaternion algebra are quadratic étale); the paper states it without proof.

items.name: The class group of a packet and its identification with Pic(Λ)
items.statement: Let S be a finite set of places containing ∞, p_1, p_2 with #G(Q)\G(A)/G(Q_S)K^S = 1, let Γ = G(Q) ∩ K^S and Y = Γ\G(Q_S) ≅ G(Q)\G(A)/K^S. Let P be the projection of [T(A)g] to Y, a finite union of periodic orbits of H = ∏_{v∈S} g_v^{-1}T(Q_v)g_v. With K_T^S := gK^Sg^{-1} ∩ T(A^S), the finite abelian group C_S := T(Q)\T(A)/T(Q_S)K_T^S acts simply transitively on the set of H-orbits in P, and all these orbits have equal mass in the push-forward of the periodic measure. With K_{T̃}^S := gO^{×,S}g^{-1} ∩ T̃(A^S), the natural map E^×\A_E^×/E_S^×K_{T̃}^S = T̃(Q)\T̃(A)/T̃(Q_S)K_{T̃}^S → C_S is an isomorphism, since its kernel Q^×\A^×/Q_S^×∏_{v∉S}Z_v^× is trivial. For finite v, K_{T̃,v} := g_vO_v^×g_v^{-1} ∩ T̃(Q_v) = Λ_v^×. Consequently C_{∞} ≅ T̃(Q)\T̃(A)/T̃(R)K_{T̃,f} ≅ Pic(Λ), where K_{T̃,f} = ∏_{v≠∞}K_{T̃,v}.
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), §2.4.2 (display (8)), §2.4.3 (display (9)) and Remark 2.7, pp. 163–167 (arXiv v3 §§2.4.2–2.4.3 and Remark 11)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): Item 9 gives only the introduction's informal version ('a quotient of the idele class group … canonical surjection onto Pic(Λ)'). The precise statements, C_S acting simply transitively, the isomorphism (9) with an S-class group of E and C_{∞} ≅ Pic(Λ), are in no item. They are the bridge from torus orbits to Picard groups that the main theorem and Section 10 use. The print writes A_E and E_S for A_E^× and E_S^× in (9), and in Remark 2.7 it has g_vO_vg_v^{-1} where O_v^× is meant.

items.name: Volume of a homogeneous toral set
items.statement: Fix a compact identity neighbourhood Ω = ∏_vΩ_v ⊂ G(A). For a homogeneous toral set [T(A)g], normalise the Haar measure on H_A = g^{-1}T(A)g so that H_A ∩ Ω has mass 1; vol([T(A)g]) is the total mass of [T(A)g] for the induced measure, equivalently vol([T(A)g]) = m_T(T(A) ∩ gΩg^{-1})^{-1} with m_T the covolume-one Haar measure on T(A). For compact identity neighbourhoods Ω, Ω', vol_Ω ≪_{Ω,Ω'} vol_{Ω'} ≪_{Ω,Ω'} vol_Ω, with constants independent of the toral set. The paper fixes Ω_v = K_v for finite v and Ω_∞ = Z(R)Ω̃_∞, a connected, compact, symmetric, Ad K_∞-invariant identity neighbourhood that equals G(R) if B is ramified at ∞. With Ω × Ω and O × O as references on G × G, vol([T^Δ(A)(g, sg)]) = vol([T(A)g]) and disc([T^Δ(A)(g, sg)]) = disc([T(A)g]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): The volume of a homogeneous toral set is a running-text definition that no item states. It fixes the reference neighbourhood Ω = ∏Ω_v used in Lemma 7.6 (item 54), in Section 8 and in the final comparison of volumes. The definition follows Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss–Michel–Venkatesh. The print writes m_T(gΩg^{-1}) for m_T(T(A) ∩ gΩg^{-1}).

items.name: The coboundary map and Hilbert 90
items.statement: Let F be a quadratic extension of Q or of Q_v, or a quadratic étale Q_v-algebra, with 𝔊 ≅ Z/2Z acting and σ the non-trivial element. Let F^{(1)} be the group of norm-one elements of F^× and O_F^{(1)} its integral elements. The coboundary map cbd : F^× → F^{(1)}, x ↦ x/^σx, is a surjective homomorphism (Hilbert's Theorem 90; directly in the split case F = Q_v × Q_v).
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), §2.1 'Notation and conventions', items (9)–(10), p. 159 (arXiv v3 §2.1)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): Defined in the conventions and used throughout Section 8 and Appendix A (cbd(Λ_v^×)\Λ_v^{(1)} ≅ H^1(𝔊, Λ_v^×), items 70, 101–107). No item defines it. The grep of items.json finds 'coboundary' only in a note. The field case is Mathlib's Hilbert 90 (Mathlib.RepresentationTheory.GroupCohomology.Hilbert90) specialised to a cyclic group of order 2; the split étale case is elementary.

items.name: A split local quaternion algebra as End_{Q_v}(E_v)
items.statement: Let v be a place with B(Q_v) split. Then ε = f·^σf for some f ∈ E_v^×. Regarding E_v as a 2-dimensional Q_v-vector space, there is an isomorphism of Q_v-algebras B(Q_v) ≅ End_{Q_v}(E_v) under which E(Q_v) ≅ E_v acts by multiplication. Explicitly, write B(Q_v) ≅ E_v ⊕ E_v by (α, β) ↦ ((α, 0), (0, ^σα)) + ((0, εβ/^σf), (^σβ/f, 0)) = ((α, βf), (^σβ/f, ^σα)) in the coordinates of Proposition 5.6. Then (α, β) acts on a ∈ E_v by (α, β).a = αa + β·^σa, through the embedding E_v ↪ E_v × E_v, a ↦ (f·a, ^σa).
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), §5.3.1, Lemma 5.10 and display (14), p. 185 (arXiv v3 Lemma 43)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): Item 92 lists 'Lemma 49 with Lemma 43' (= Lemmas 5.16 and 5.10) as its locator but states only Lemma 5.16. The identification B(Q_v) ≅ End_{Q_v}(E_v), in which End_{Z_v}(Λ_v) in items 38 and 39 is computed, appears in no item's statement. Alternatively, extend item 92 or item 38. Used in the proofs of Lemma 5.11, Proposition 5.12 and Proposition 5.15.

items.name: Volume of a homogeneous Hecke set
items.statement: For ξ ∈ (G × G)(A), vol([G^Δ(A)ξ]) := m_{G^Δ}(G^Δ(A) ∩ ξ(Ω × Ω)ξ^{-1})^{-1} = m_G(Ω ∩ ctr(ξ)Ωctr(ξ)^{-1})^{-1}, where m_G = m_{G^Δ} is the covolume-one Haar measure and Ω is the fixed reference neighbourhood of §2.4.5. The volume of a simply connected homogeneous Hecke set is defined analogously. The map ξ ↦ vol([G^Δ(A)ξ]) is continuous from (G × G)(A) to R_{>0} and factors through ctr : (G × G)(A) → G(A).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): A running-text definition that Lemma 7.6 (item 54) and Proposition 7.8 (item 56) compute with. No item states it. The second equality uses unimodularity and the substitution h = ξ_1^{-1}gξ_1.

items.name: The 2-torsion of the Picard group of an imaginary quadratic order
items.statement: Let Λ be an imaginary quadratic order of discriminant D. Let μ_tame be the number of odd primes dividing D, and μ_wild := ord_2[Z_2^× : Nr Λ_2^×] ∈ {0,1,2}; μ_wild depends only on 𝔣_2 and on the ramification of 2 in E. Then #Pic(Λ)[2] = [Pic(Λ) : Pic(Λ)²] = 2^{μ_tame+μ_wild−1} ≍ 2^{ω(D)}. The first equality follows from the exact sequence 1 → Pic(Λ)[2] → Pic(Λ) → Pic(Λ)² → 1 (squaring); the second from Corollary A.2 and Lemma A.6.
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), Appendix A.1, Corollary A.7, p. 260 (arXiv v3 Corollary 160)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): The size of Pic(Λ)[2] and the exponent μ_wild. μ_wild enters the weight r of Definition 8.6 (item 59), and Pic(Λ)[2] bounds the fibres in Corollary 8.28 (item 70). Suggested owner: HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.0, with items 101–107. The maximal-order case (2-rank = t − 1 for imaginary K) is planned by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic Layer 3.

items.name: 2-torsion in Pic(Λ) through local Galois cohomology
items.statement: Let Λ be an imaginary quadratic order, 𝔊 = Gal(E/Q), cbd(x) = x/^σx, and let Λ^{(1)}, Λ_v^{(1)} be the norm-one units. The diagonal restriction map H^1(𝔊, Λ^×) → ∏_{v≠∞} H^1(𝔊, Λ_v^×) is injective, and there is a canonical isomorphism H^1(𝔊,Λ^×)\∏_{v≠∞} H^1(𝔊, Λ_v^×) ≅ Pic(Λ)[2]. Consequently ∏_{v≠∞}[Λ_v^{(1)} : cbd(Λ_v^×)] = ∏_{v≠∞} #H^1(𝔊, Λ_v^×) = 2·#Pic(Λ)[2], using H^1(𝔊,L) ≅ L^{(1)}/cbd(L^×) and [Λ^{(1)} : cbd(Λ^×)] = 2.
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), Appendix A.3, Proposition A.11 and Corollary A.12, pp. 261–263 (arXiv v3 Proposition 164, Corollary 165)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): The cohomological description of Pic(Λ)[2] that gives #inv^{-1}(inv([h])) ≪ #Pic(Λ)[2] (Corollary 8.28, item 70). It is a different result from the principal genus theorem of item 106. Suggested owner: HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.0. Inputs: Hilbert 90 for E and E_v (tauceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9), Pic(Z) = 1, and Z^× ∩ Nr E^× = 1 for imaginary E.

items.name: The small part of the discriminant and the genus weights
items.statement: Fix C_θ ≥ 1 with C_θ^{-1}X ≤ Σ_{p≤X} log p ≤ C_θX for all X ∈ N (Chebyshev), and 1/2 > η > 0. Write D = D_small·D_large, where D_small := ∏_{p ∥ D, p ∤ ω, 2 < p ≤ (η/(4C_θ))·log|D|} p; then D_small ≤ |D|^{η/4}. Put k := υp_1^{2n}D_small², so that Z/kZ = Z/υZ × Z/p_1^{2n}Z × ∏_{p|D_small} Z/p²Z. For p | D_small, partition Z/p²Z = C_{+0} ⊔ C_{−0} ⊔ C_{+1} ⊔ C_{−1} ⊔ C_2, where C_{±0} := {u ∈ (Z/p²Z)^× : (u/p) = ±1}, C_{±1} := {pu : u ∈ (Z/pZ)^×, (u/p) = ±1} and C_2 := {0}. Let w_p be the measure on Z/p²Z that is uniform on each atom, with w_p(C_{±0}) = #C_{±0} = (p²/2)(1 − 1/p) and w_p(C_2) = 2. For ε ∈ {±1}, w_p(C_ε) = 2·#C_ε = p(1 − 1/p) if χ_p(Nr(p_1^n𝔰𝔢)) = −ε, and w_p(C_ε) = 0 otherwise. Set w_k := δ_{0 mod υ} × δ_{0 mod p_1^{2n}} × ∏_{p|D_small} w_p on Z/kZ. For m ∈ Z/kZ, D_i(m) := ∏_{p|D_small, ord_p m = i} p (Definition 10.9, item 95).
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), §10.2, pp. 242–243 (running text before Lemma 10.6); arXiv v3 §10.2, before Lemma 144
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (coverage of the published text): Definitions used in Lemma 10.6 and Propositions 10.10–10.15 (items 91, 94–100). No item states them; item 94 refers to w_k and item 91 to D_large. Suggested owner: GeometryOfNumbersPartIIToralJoinings (route 1), with items 94–100. The factor 2 on the classes outside C_{±0} comes from r; the zero weight on one of C_{±1} is the genus restriction (Proposition A.10).

items.name: The ideal-counting function of a quadratic order is of class M(A,B,ε)
items.statement: Let Λ be an imaginary quadratic order with conductor 𝔣, and f(n) := #{𝔞 ∈ 𝒥(Λ) : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ, Nr 𝔞 = n}. For every ε > 0 there are 1 ≤ A ≪_𝔣 1 and 0 < B ≪_{ε,𝔣} 1 such that f ∈ M(A,B,ε), i.e. 0 ≤ f(n) ≤ min(A^{Ω(n)}, B·n^ε) for all n ≥ 1. Moreover f(pn) = f(n) for p ∥ D (p ∤ 𝔣), and f(k_1) = 1 when k_1 is supported on ramified primes coprime to 𝔣.
items.locator: Annals 189 (2019), §10.3, proof of Proposition 10.10, pp. 245–246 (arXiv v3 proof of Proposition 148)

It is asserted in running text without a numbered statement. Proved from the Euler product of ζ_E, modified at the primes dividing 𝔣. items.name: The main theorem in the range of large minimal ideal norm
items.statement: Assume the hypotheses of Theorem 3.2: G a form of PGL_2 over Q; K_∞ < G(R) a maximal compact torus; p_1, p_2 primes; H_i = [T_i^Δ(A)(g_i,s_ig_i)] with g_∞^{-1}T_i(R)g_∞ = K_∞, p_1 and p_2 split in E_i, no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero for ζ_{E_i}, bounded conductors 𝔣_i, |D_i| → ∞, and, for every compact B ⊂ G(A), g_i^{-1}T_i(Q)s_ig_i ∩ B = ∅ for i ≫_B 1. Let θ_l be an admissible exponent and 𝔑_i := min{Nr 𝔞 : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ_i, [𝔞] = [𝔰_i]}. Suppose there is η_0 > 0 with 𝔑_i ≥ |D_i|^{(2−θ_l^{-1})/3+η_0} for all i ≫ 1 (condition (55)). Then for every ξ ∈ (G×G)(A), every n ∈ N and i ≫_{ξ,n} 1, Cor[μ_i, ν_ξ](B^{(−n,n)}) ≪_{G,𝔣} vol([G^Δ(A)^+ξ])^{-1}·κ(ξ)·|ω(ξ)|²·(log log(2|ω(ξ)|))^8·p_1^{−4n}, with κ, ω as in Theorem 8.7. Consequently, by Lemma 10.1 with ρ = 1, every weak-* limit of μ_i is (G×G)(A)^+-invariant. Ingredients: Lemma 10.4 turns (55) into R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−4η} for some η = η(η_0,θ_l) > 0. The no-exceptional-zero hypothesis gives L′/L(1,χ_{E_i}) ≤ C·log|D_{E_i}| with C independent of i (Hecke, via Landau [Lan18]). Then Theorem 8.7, Proposition 10.15 and the class number formula for vol([T(A)g]) apply. Finally, ξ ↦ vol([G^Δ(A)^+ξ]) is bounded below by a non-vanishing continuous function of ctr(ξ), because the fibres of ctr on G^Δ(A)^+\(G×G)(A) are compact.

items.name: The main theorem in the range of small minimal ideal norm, by Linnik's method
items.statement: Assume the hypotheses of Theorem 3.2, and let θ be a bound towards the Ramanujan conjecture for SL_2 in the sense of Clozel–Ullmo. Input: for j ∈ {1,2}, m ∈ N and U = ∏_p U_p < G^{sc}(A_f) compact open, with U_{p_j} the intersection of two Iwahori subgroups in the apartment of A_{p_j} and K_{p_j} ⊇ U_{p_j} maximal compact, the Hecke operator T_{p_j^m} on L²([G^{sc}(A)])^U satisfies ‖T_{p_j^m}‖_0 ≪_{U^{p_j},p_j,ε} [K_{p_j} : U_{p_j}]·p_j^{−m(1−θ+ε)/2} on the orthocomplement of the constants. This follows from decay of matrix coefficients and Jacquet–Langlands. Claim: if there is ε_1 > 0 with 𝔑_i ≤ |D_i|^{1/(2+2/(1−θ)) − ε_1} for all i ≫ 1 (condition (59)), then every weak-* limit μ of μ_i satisfies ∫ f dμ = 0 for every smooth compactly supported f ∈ L²_00([(G×G)(A)]) invariant at p_1 under an intersection of two Iwahori subgroups in the apartment of A_{p_1}. Bootstrapping through maximal entropy for a^Δ, μ is then (G×G)(A)^+-invariant. The argument is that of Ellenberg–Michel–Venkatesh [EMV13, §3], with the effective equidistribution of [Kha17, §5] and Linnik's basic lemma for one-sided Bowen balls in the range 𝔑_i·p_1^m ≤ |D|^{1/2+o(1)}. The ranges (55) and (59) overlap as soon as θ_l < 2/3 or θ < 1/2: at θ_l = 2/3 and θ = 1/2 both thresholds equal 1/6, and Huxley's admissible θ_l > 131/208 gives 18/131 < 1/6.
